final.summary:
Final implementation plan as of 2026-10-13, corrected after two critiques. This was research only: I edited nothing in the repo, pushed no kernels and made no submissions. Every repo change below is a proposal for whoever builds it. The user asked to start building once the plan is ready, so Stage 0 (CPU only) is the first build step.

ORDER (cheapest decisive check first)
0. CPU prep: fix the dev kernel for the 10-12 harness, add capture, adapter and paired-eval tools, prove capture on a mock, check the 31B training shards. 0 GPU h.
1. FT-0, about 0.75 h of 4xL4. A dummy r16 adapter on the exact scorer stack at gmu 0.80 and 0.90: does it start, keep its KV cache, change the logits, and survive a 16k prompt_logprobs call? This gates the whole fine-tuning track.
2. T0, about 2.9 h, run in parallel with 1. Thinking-on config v3t_think on all 33 dev tasks with capture on. It sets the 12 h runtime projection, smoke-tests capture on live vLLM, and becomes the prompt-only submission. Public thinking-on configs score 0.17-0.18 against our 0.12, so this is the step most likely to raise the score.
3. Data pass 1 on the 72 train tasks, about 5.9 h. Pre-registered stop: if fewer than 15 distinct tasks resolve, stop the FT track. Pass 2 can only re-sample tasks already solved, so the 15-task gate would be unreachable. Pass 2 is expected to run, about 3.6 h.
4. Convert captures into loss-masked examples (CPU).
5. Train an r16 QLoRA, about 3.25 h, week 2.
6. FT-0R plus E0 parity with the trained adapter in its own short notebook, about 0.5 h. This gates the dev runs.
7. Paired LoRA-vs-control dev runs on one LoRA-enabled server. E1 then E2, about 4.2 h each; E2 runs only if E1 passes its early stop.
8. Submit only on GO, and keep an adapter-free hedge.

DECISIONS
- Thinking ON: thinking_config {include_thoughts: true, thinking_budget: 4096}, max_output_tokens 8192, budgets 5.0 min / 30 calls / 80 turns / timeout 180.
  - Evidence: the 129-task sweep resolved 23 with thinking off vs 48-51 with it on (746250), and every public 0.17-0.18 config has thinking on.
  - Our 'off' config v3b_noedit now runs thinking-on with thoughts stripped on adk 0.2.13 (generation.py:403-417, limits.py:400-438, swegemma/config.py:59-67). That was the 35/129 mode in the sweep.
- Model: 31B gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct, trained on its bf16 QAT checkpoint qat-q4_0-unquantized/2.
- Adapter: r16, alpha 32, all 7 projections of the language model only. The global-layer k_proj LoRA is duplicated as v_proj.
- Data: rejection sampling of our own runs through a proxy that logs vLLM's exact token ids. Stronger teachers add little (747168).
- Decision: paired, pre-registered GO rule.

WHAT CHANGED AFTER THE CRITIQUES (all blocking items applied)
1) E0 parity OOM (critique 1). I checked this in vLLM source:
   - gpu_model_runner.py:5062-5071 computes full-vocabulary logits plus an fp32 log_softmax for every prefill chunk of a prompt_logprobs request.
   - The default max_num_batched_tokens is 2048 on GPUs under 70 GiB (arg_utils.py:2063-2068).
   - prompt_logprobs requests skip the prefix cache (sampling_params.py:420-425).
   Fixes:
   - FT-0 test (e) now sends a 16,384-token token-id prompt with prompt_logprobs=0 as the last test on each server, at 0.80 and 0.90, and records survival and peak memory.
   - E0 moved out of the dev-run notebooks into its own 0.5 h notebook (Stage 6) that runs before any dev run. If (e) failed, it uses --max-num-batched-tokens 512 via VllmConfig.extra_args (server.py:160, 800), and falls back to 4,096-token slices that Stage 5 also scores in HF.
2) GO rule too weak and controls pooled across weeks (critique 2).
   - LoRA and control now run as paired variants in the same notebook on the same LoRA-enabled server. The adapter is mounted in both and referenced only in the LoRA variant, which agent_eval.py:147-157 already requires.
   - 4 pairs (E1 + E2), with no cross-week pooling.
   - GO needs a mean paired gain of at least +1.5 tasks per run AND an exact one-sided McNemar p ≤ 0.05 on discordant task-run cells, plus safety checks.
3) Dev-run cost (critique 2). The decision set leaves out:
   - the 15 unfair tasks (0 of 75 historical passes);
   - the fixable tasks never solved: fastapi_13920, fastapi_14986, rich_4075, rich_4076. Each was 0/6 across v3b_noedit, v3b_r2, v3b_r3, v2a_rerun and v3e ×2 (computed from eval/runs/**/task_results.jsonl). A task is dropped only if Stage 2 also fails it.
   That gives dev_dec of about 14 tasks. This goes further than the critique's 18 tasks, because it is what keeps a 2.85 h reserve in week 2. If training moves to Lightning, use all 18.
   Stage 2's thinking-on run stays on all 33 tasks because the runtime projection needs the tasks that hit the cap.
4) Thinking decision rule (critique 2).
   - The thinking-off arm is dropped. With one run per arm it had a 17-20% chance of a noise flip, and it changed budgets as well as thinking.
   - ON is the deployment setting. A matched-budget off check (v3t_off: same budgets, thinking_budget 0) runs only if Stage 2 shows a problem. Switching to OFF needs off ≥ on + 3 confirmed by a second paired run.
5) Budget slack (critique 2).
   - Pass 2 is budgeted as expected, not conditional.
   - The pass-1 stop rule is explicit.
   - The training guard is cut to 2.75 h.
   - Reserves: 1.85 h of 4xL4 in week 1 and 2.85 h in week 2.

Non-blocking items, all adopted:
- The capture proxy is wired into the MODEL_URL branch too, and the mock returns token ids, so the Stage 0 mock test really exercises capture.
- If S2 fails with the sampler-warmup OOM from 746503, go straight to the stop branch. Rank changes do not affect that cost.
- New span categories: content_reordered and empty_thought_dropped (verified in chat_template.jinja:237-240 and 300-353). For a content-reordered call, only the thought and tool call are labelled, never the trailing '<turn|>'.
- A thought cut off at the budget (vLLM builtin.py:465-550 forces '<channel|>') has that thought masked.
- The loss code is correct as written. The earlier 'shift' note is removed.
- Overflow is checked per call.
- The summarizer runs through the adapter in the LoRA arms.
- A 2-minute NF4 smoke test runs before the 62.6 GB load.
- The prompt-only submission is gated only on: finished, 0 overflow, core ≥ 5/6, projection ≤ 10.5 h.
- env.json records the wheelhouse sizes for every run.
- Explicit stop conditions after FT-0, pass 1, E0 and E1.

BUDGET
- Re-verified with `kaggle quota` on 2026-10-13 at 04:08 UTC: 30.00 GPU h, 0 used, refresh 2026-10-17 00:00 UTC.
- 4xL4 bills at 2x (docs/competition.md:132-133; forum 748500), so that is about 15 h of 4xL4 wall time per week.
- Week 1: 13.15 h + 1.85 h reserve. Week 2: 12.15 h + 2.85 h reserve, assuming the quota resets to 30.

USER ACTIONS
- Create the private datasets: gemma-ft-wheels, gemma-ft-sft, gemma-ft-adapter.
- Make every submission (1 pending at most; the queue is about 33 h).
- Run `kaggle quota` before each launch.

Scratch evidence and reusable code are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaggle-finetune-gemma/16026f0c-2bda-5281-bad9-92d73f9dba6b/scratchpad/ft_research/:

- compute/ft0_lora_check.py, compute/make_dummy_adapter.py
- fix_k_eq_v.py, validate_adapter.py, dequant_ct.py
- kwh_1012/ (the 10-12 wheels, the diffs, scripts/tail.py, rangefetch.py)
- khcache/.../gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct/2/ (the served chat_template.jinja and tokenizer)

Adapter
adapter_tools.make_dummy(rank=16, dup_k_as_v=True), with lora_A ~ N(0,1)/sqrt(in), lora_B ~ N(0,0.02) and alpha 32. Both A and B are nonzero, which rules out the zero-weight confound in Fawad07's 10-08 test (743508).

Servers, in order
Each is started as the scorer path does: discover_adapters + VllmServer(VllmConfig(..., enable_lora=True, max_loras=8, max_lora_rank=128, gpu_memory_utilization=G)). build_cmd then emits --enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 16 --lora-modules ft0_r16=<dir> (server.py:781-791).

- S1_r16_090: G = 0.90, the adk 0.2.13 default; the scorer may use this one.
- S2p (only if test (e) killed S2): G = 0.80 + VLLM_EXTRA_ARGS ["--max-num-batched-tokens","512"]. Runs test (e) only.
- S2b_r8_080 (only if S2 fails to start for a reason OTHER than the sampler-warmup OOM of forum 746503, e.g. too little KV). A warmup OOM goes straight to the stop branch: its cost scales with max_num_seqs times the 262k vocabulary, not with rank (an r16 slot is about 0.11 GiB per GPU).
The no-adapter reference server is dropped: base vs adapter is compared on the same server.

Tests per server, riskiest last so an engine crash loses nothing

(a) A 28k-token prompt + 256 output tokens on both names, timeout 600 s.

stages.success_criteria:
FT-0 PASS needs all of:
- S2 starts with --enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 16 and no 'CUDA out of memory occurred when warming up sampler'.
- 'Maximum concurrency for 32,768 tokens per request' is at least 1.0x at 0.80. Record the KV tokens (Fawad07 saw 27,696 with an r4 adapter).
- The 28k prompt completes on both names.
- base vs base and adapter vs adapter first-token logprob differences are < 1e-3, while base vs adapter text differs or the difference is > 0.05.
- Adapter decode is >= 85% of base-name decode on the same server.

Also record test (e) at 0.80 and 0.90: survived or OOM, plus peak memory. (e) is not a PASS condition. It decides how Stage 6 runs parity.
stages.failure_fallback:
- Sampler-warmup OOM, or no start at 0.80: stop the fine-tuning track and spend nothing on Stage 3. Post the repro on 746503 and 743508 and ask the organizers which gmu and max-num-seqs the scorer uses. Continue with the prompt-only config.
- Adapter not applied (identical logprobs): stop the track and report the same way.
- (e) OOMs at 16k even on S2p: Stage 6 computes parity on 4,096-token slices (sft_val_slices.jsonl), which Stage 5 also scores in HF.
- S2 fails for a non-warmup reason but S2b passes: train r8 with the same targets.

stages.name: Stage 3 - Data generation: rejection-sample our own 31B agent on the 72 train tasks with config D
stages.goal:
Produce token-exact trajectories that pass the hidden tests on train tasks, generated by exactly the served model, prompt, budgets, thinking mode and compaction that will be deployed.
Start only after Stage 1 PASS and with Stage 2's config D fixed.
Why self-generated: stronger teachers add little on this harness. In 747168, the union of 4 model runs was 73/123, and the teachers solved only 10 of the 60 tasks Gemma failed twice.
What it teaches: rejection-sampling fine-tuning (self-distillation on verified successes), and how per-task pass rate and cost per pass set the data budget.

stages.name: Stage 4 - Convert captures to loss-masked SFT examples and run data QA (CPU)
stages.goal:
Turn captures into training sequences whose text is exactly what the served model saw, with labels only on what the model itself sampled, and with explicit handling of every way the history re-render differs from the raw sample.
What it teaches:
- Chat templates and special tokens (<|channel>, <|tool_call>, stop tokens 50 and 106).
- Loss masking.
- Why compaction splits a trajectory into segments.
- Forced end-of-thinking.
- Filtering, dedupe and per-task caps.

LAYOUT (inside submission.zip)

- Nothing else goes under adapters/: delete PEFT's README.md, and ship no tokenizer files.

- For a paired dev run, every variant mounts the same adapters, and only the LoRA variant references one.

adapter_config.json
PEFT 0.21.2 writes extra fields; vLLM reads only those marked "used". Assert these values after save:
{
  "peft_type": "LORA",
  "task_type": "CAUSAL_LM",
  "base_model_name_or_path": "<any string; ignored by vLLM and the harness>",
  "r": 16,                    // used: --max-lora-rank = bucket(16) = 16 (adk server.py:58-67, 781-791); adk_submission also reads r
  "lora_alpha": 32,           // used: scaling = 32/16 = 2
  "lora_dropout": 0.0,
  "bias": "none",             // required by PEFTHelper
  "use_dora": false,          // required
  "use_rslora": false,
  "modules_to_save": null,    // required
  "target_modules": "<the regex below, JSON-escaped>",   // must exist; vLLM does not use its content for matching
  "rank_pattern": {},
  "alpha_pattern": {}         // both must stay empty: vLLM ignores them, so outputs would be mis-scaled
}
Training regex (Python raw string): r".*language_model.*\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)"

adapter_model.safetensors
Format: bf16, metadata {"format": "pt"}, 840 tensors, about 236 MiB at r16.
Keys, for N in 0..59:
- base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.self_attn.{q_proj,k_proj,o_proj}.lora_{A,B}.weight
- base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.self_attn.v_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight
  - N not in G: trained.
  - N in G = {5,11,17,23,29,35,41,47,53,59}: a CLONE of that layer's k_proj lora_A/lora_B, written by dup_k_as_v.
- base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.mlp.{gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj}.lora_{A,B}.weight

Shapes: lora_A [r, in], lora_B [out, r].
- Sliding layers (N not in G): q 5376->8192, k 5376->4096, v 5376->4096, o 8192->5376.
- Global layers (N in G): q 5376->16384, k 5376->2048, v (duplicate) 5376->2048, o 16384->5376.
- MLP: gate/up 5376->21504, down 21504->5376.
- Count: 410 trained modules (820 tensors) + 20 duplicated tensors = 840.

Why the duplicate
- On the k_eq_v layers, HF computes V = k_proj(x) including the LoRA delta (modeling_gemma4.py:1225-1271).
- vLLM copies the base k_proj weights into the V slot of qkv_proj, but applies a V-slot LoRA only from a v_proj entry (gemma4.py:1649-1660; lora/model_manager.py:632-668).
- Duplicating the k_proj LoRA as v_proj makes vLLM compute V = (W_k + 2·B_k·A_k)x, exactly as in training.
- Validated with vLLM's loader logic on CPU (scratch fix_k_eq_v.py + validate_adapter.py). The first GPU confirmation is FT-0 with the dummy adapter and FT-0R with the real one.

How vLLM maps and serves it (patched wheelhouse vLLM 0.19.1 only; stock PyPI 0.19.1 refuses LoRA on this model)
- parse_fine_tuned_lora_name strips 'base_model.model.'. The gemma4_mm hf_to_vllm_mapper maps 'model.language_model.' to 'language_model.model.'. q/k/v pack into qkv_proj and gate/up into gate_up_proj.
- Forbidden: any vision key (`.linear`, input_proj), embed_tokens, lm_head, embed_vision.
  - PEFT 'all-linear' adds these.
  - The plain 7-name list fails on Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration (PEFT raises on Gemma4ClippableLinear).
  - So use the regex.
- Flags emitted by adk_submission 0.2.13 build_cmd: --enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 16 --lora-modules main_lora=<dir>, plus --no-scheduler-reserve-full-isl. LiteLLM model id: openai/main_lora; alias adapter:main_lora.
- Memory, computed from source, not measured: about 0.11 GiB of LoRA buffer per GPU for one r16 slot.
- Prompt-logprob requests (used only by E0) need extra, unprofiled memory for full-vocabulary logits. Stage 1 test (e) measures it.

Validation before every upload or submission
- validate(dir, real=True): replicates PEFTHelper, the name mapper, the unexpected-module check and the 31B shapes.
- discover_adapters(<submission dir>) must return exactly {main_lora: rank 16}.
- No key may contain 'vision', 'embed' or 'lm_head'.
- FT-0R (Stage 6) must pass on the uploaded files.

Fallback layout
- r8 with the same targets. Use it only if FT-0 shows a non-warmup startup failure at r16; rank does not change the sampler-warmup OOM cost.
- Attention-only regex r".*language_model.*\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj)" + dup. Use it only for the same reason.

- Image: gcr.io/kaggle-private-byod/python@sha256:37c64f7d… (= kaggle-gpu-images v170). Python 3.12, CUDA 12.8.1, torch 2.10.0+cu128, datasets 5.0.0, huggingface-hub 1.11.0.

- transformers 5.13.1 + peft 0.21.2 is verified on a tiny Gemma4 model (scratch tiny/). bnb 0.46.1 + torch 2.10 is checked by the step-0 NF4 smoke test.
- Not used:
  - trl: the template has no generation tags, and the data is pre-tokenized.
  - liger-kernel: its lm_head would sit on a different device under device_map.
  - unsloth: pins transformers 5.5.0.
  - flash-attn: the global head_dim is 512.

STEP 0: NF4 SMOKE TEST (about 2 min, before the 62.6 GB load)
- bnb.nn.Linear4bit(5376, 21504, quant_type='nf4', compute_dtype=bf16) forward and backward on cuda:0.
- A tiny Gemma4 (from_config: 2 layers, hidden 256), saved and reloaded with the BitsAndBytesConfig below, wrapped with PEFT, one step with finite grads.

BASE MODEL
- Path: /kaggle/input/models/google/gemma-4/transformers/gemma-4-31b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized/2 (62.6 GB bf16; Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration).
- Why: it is the QAT checkpoint the served ct model was re-quantized from. cos(ct, qat) = 0.9982 vs 0.9935 to gemma-4-31b-it bf16.
- Stage 0 checks that the shards are complete.

LOADING
- bnb = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
- model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(P, quantization_config=bnb, dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', device_map='auto', max_memory={0:'16GiB', 1:'21GiB', 2:'21GiB', 3:'21GiB'})
- model.config.use_cache = False; freeze all parameters; model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={'use_reentrant': False}).
- Do NOT call prepare_model_for_kbit_training: it upcasts the 1.41B-parameter embedding to fp32.
- Keep the vision tower loaded. It is never called on text, and loading it keeps the PEFT key names vLLM expects.
- No tokenizer is needed: the data is vLLM token ids.

LoRA CONFIG
- LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.0, bias='none', use_dora=False, use_rslora=False, task_type='CAUSAL_LM', target_modules=r'.*language_model.*\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)')
- Assert 410 LoRA modules (60 layers × 7, minus the 10 missing global v_proj), about 121-123M trainable parameters, and no 'vision' in any name.
- fp32 master weights; Adam states about 1.9 GB.

LOSS (custom, chunked, softcapped, labelled positions only)
def lm_loss_sum(model, ids, labels, chunk=1024):
    base = model.get_base_model()
    h = base.model(input_ids=ids, use_cache=False).last_hidden_state   # [1, S, 5376]
    tgt = labels[:, 1:]                                # h[:, j] predicts token j+1 == tgt[:, j]
    idx = (tgt[0] != -100).nonzero().squeeze(-1)      # correct as written; do NOT shift idx again
    W = base.lm_head.weight                            # tied embedding, on GPU0
    hs, y = h[0, idx].to(W.device), tgt[0, idx].to(W.device)
    def ce(hc, yc):
        z = torch.tanh((hc @ W.T).float() / 30.0) * 30.0     # final_logit_softcapping = 30
        return F.cross_entropy(z, yc, reduction='sum')
    return sum(checkpoint(ce, hs[i:i+chunk], y[i:i+chunk], use_reentrant=False)
               for i in range(0, len(y), chunk)), len(y)
Fail-fast check (i): loss_sum / n must match HF model(ids, labels=labels).loss within 1e-2 on a 1k-token slice.

LOOP AND HYPERPARAMETERS
- AdamW(trainable, lr=1e-4, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-8, weight_decay=0.0, fused=True); fallback foreach=True.
  - 1e-4 follows the usual QLoRA setting for 30B-class models (an assumption). 2e-4 is the round-2 option.
- Micro-batch 1 sequence, no padding, no packing.
- Gradient accumulation over 4 sequences, token-weighted: n = labelled tokens in the group, and each sequence does (loss_sum / n).backward().
- clip_grad_norm_(trainable, 1.0).
- Schedule: linear warmup 3 steps, then cosine to 10% of peak.
- 1 epoch (2 only if the data is <= 0.5M tokens). About 20-27 optimizer steps for 80-110 segments.
- max_len 16,384 (Stage 4 truncates); seed 0; shuffle by segment.
- Time guard: stop and save once training time exceeds 2.75 h.
- Val NLL at step 0 and at the end, on sft_val (full) and sft_val_slices (4k windows). Stage 6 compares against these.
- Log every step: loss, labelled tokens, tok/s, torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated per GPU.

FAIL-FAST BEFORE THE LONG LOOP
(i) The loss parity check above.
(ii) One optimizer step at the longest sequence.
(iii) A step-0 adapter saves and passes dup_k_as_v + validate(real=True).
(iv) Step-0 val NLL is finite.

EXPORT (at the guard and at the end)
- model.save_pretrained(OUT, safe_serialization=True)
- Cast all tensors to bf16 and delete README.md.
- dup_k_as_v(OUT) adds 20 v_proj tensors on layers 5, 11, …, 59.
- validate(OUT, real=True).
- Write train_log.json.

EXPECTED COST (estimates, unmeasured)
- About 120 tok/s at 16k on 4xL4 naive model parallel, so about 2.3 h per 1M tokens.

OPTIONAL LIGHTNING VARIANT

final.data_spec:
SOURCE
- Our own agent: gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct served by the wheelhouse's patched vLLM 0.19.1 (re-patched 10-12) on Kaggle 4xL4, TP4, GMU 0.90, no adapter. Harness: adk_submission 0.2.13, swegemma 0.2.11, google-adk 1.36.1.
- Config D = experiments/v3t_think unless Stage 2 changes it:
  - temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64, max_output_tokens 8192;
  - thinking {include_thoughts: true, thinking_budget: 4096};
  - budgets 5.0 min / 30 calls / 80 turns / timeout 180.
- Compaction 14336/15/2/5, concurrency 1.
- Tasks: the 72 tasks of eval/splits.json['train'] (fastapi 41, rich 28, requests 3). Never dev (33) and never excluded_unhealthy (24).
- Every run's env.json must show the same wheel sizes as Stage 2. If the wheelhouse changes mid-plan, redo the Stage 2 capture checks before mixing data.

CAPTURE
- kaggle/common/capture_proxy.py sits between LiteLLM and vLLM (port 8001 to 8000). It adds return_token_ids and strips the token-id fields before the response goes back to the agent.
- One gzip JSON line per call in captures/<variant>/<instance_id>.jsonl.gz: seq, kind (agent/summarizer/other), http_status, request body, response body, prompt_token_ids, completion_token_ids.
- Size: about 50-180 MB per pass (estimate).

SAMPLING PLAN
- Pass 1: 1 sample per task (2 shards of 36 in parallel).
- Gate: if fewer than 15 distinct tasks resolve, stop the fine-tuning track.
- Pass 2 (expected): 2 more samples (variants g2, g3) on up to 25 tasks resolved in pass 1.
- Per-task cap: 3 kept trajectories.

FILTERS (trajectory level)
- resolved == True and error empty;
- submit_patch was called and a final text answer exists;
- no continuation nudge (a user message after the first that does not start with 'For context:');
- no finish_reason 'length';
- no garbled '<|tool_call>' text, no 'mandatory input parameters are not present', and no tool-error responses from the swegemma 0.2.11 ToolErrorPlugin;
- at most 2 exact consecutive repeats of a call;
- the patch touches library source only (swegemma 0.2.11 also strips test, conftest and config edits);
- dedupe identical completion-token sequences and identical normalized patches, keeping the shorter trajectory;
- cap 3 per task, preferring fewer calls and distinct patches;
- assert instance_id is in the train split.

EXAMPLE CONSTRUCTION
- Agent records only: summarizer records are dropped, and retries of an identical prompt are collapsed.
- A new segment starts whenever the messages list stops growing by pure appending (compaction).
- Sequence = P_last + C_last: vLLM's prompt_token_ids of the segment's last request plus its completion_token_ids.
- Each earlier completion C_i is located in P_last as the tokens after prefix P_i, up to and including the next stop token (50 or 106). It is then classified against the raw C_i as exact, ws_only, argorder, content_reordered, empty_thought_dropped or other.

LABELS
Labelled (token ids):
- the model-sampled spans: the thought block, then '<|tool_call>…<tool_call|>' + token 50, then the final '…<turn|>' (106);
- earlier calls take the rendered thought and tool call as located (exact, ws_only, argorder).
Masked (-100):
- content_reordered calls: the trailing content and '<turn|>' (the thought and tool call stay labelled);
- calls whose thought reached the 4,096 budget: the thought and the forced '<channel|>' (the tool call stays labelled);
- system prompt and tools block;
- task, nudge and 'For context' summary messages;
- tool-response bodies;
- newlines after <turn|>;
- assistant turns retained across a compaction.
Thinking ON: generation prompts end at '<|turn>model' + newline with no empty-thought block, so nothing is re-inserted. Thinking OFF (fallback only): re-insert the masked empty thought as in scratch convert_captures.py.
Truncation: if a sequence is longer than 16,384, cut at the last labelled stop token at or below 16,384. Drop it if no labelled call remains.

FILES
data/sft/v1/ (uploaded by the user as private dataset <owner>/gemma-ft-sft):
- sft_train.jsonl
- sft_val.jsonl: 1 trajectory from each of up to 5 tasks with >= 3 kept. Used only for NLL and E0 parity, not as a generalization test.
- sft_val_slices.jsonl: the same, cut into 4,096-token windows.
- stats.json
Each line: {input_ids, labels, meta:{variant, instance_id, segment_idx, calls, exact, ws_only, argorder, content_reordered, empty_thought_dropped, forced_think_end, other, unlocated, n_tokens, n_labelled, truncated}}

GATES
- >= 40 trajectories from >= 15 tasks.
- unlocated = 0 and other = 0.
- forced_think_end <= 10% of calls.
- < 15% of labelled tokens lost to truncation.

EXPECTED SIZE (estimates; re-plan after pass 1)
- 45-60 kept trajectories over 20-25 tasks.
- 70-110 segments.
- 0.8-1.3M tokens in total; max about 22.5k before truncation (14.3k prompt + up to 8k completion).
- The labelled share is higher than with thinking off because thoughts are labelled. The thinking-off reference was about 2.3k labelled tokens per trajectory.

KNOWN BIASES
- About 13 easy tasks dominate (hence the cap).
- Only about 1 in 5 successes involves compaction.
- The hidden test repos differ from the 4 public ones (admin, 747248), so overfitting to repo specifics is possible.
- Some public tasks need names the issue does not state (748482).

open_risks: LoRA effect on the current scorer build is unconfirmed. Fawad07 (743508, 10-08) saw identical logprobs with noise adapters. No team has shown a LoRA submission scoring above its base, and the one published trained-LoRA test was a NO-GO (2/32 vs 4/32). FT-0 (dummy adapter) and FT-0R (trained adapter) gate the track.

The scorer's vLLM flags are not visible: scripts/inference.py is not public. gpu_memory_utilization may be 0.80 (HARNESS_README:165) or 0.90 (the adk 0.2.13 default). An r16 all-linear adapter OOMed in sampler warmup at 0.80 (746503) and was fixed only by --max-num-seqs, which a submission cannot set. FT-0 tests both values. A warmup OOM stops the track; lowering the rank would not help.

E0 parity memory: prompt_logprobs computes full-vocabulary logits for every prefill chunk on every TP rank, and the profiler does not count this (gpu_model_runner.py:5062-5071; max_num_batched_tokens defaults to 2048 on L4, arg_utils.py:2063-2068). Stage 1 test (e) measures it. E0 runs in its own 0.5 h notebook, so an OOM can no longer cost a dev run.

The thinking-on gain at about 5-min caps has never been measured in a controlled run on our harness. We commit to ON based on external evidence (746250; all public 0.17-0.18 configs), and run a thinking-off check only if Stage 2 shows a problem. If thinking-on were in fact neutral here (yiyu, 747696), both the data and the deployment would cost more time for no gain.

12 h scorer limit: the worst case is 120 × (5.0 + 0.5) min + 0.2 h ≈ 11.2 h, and the hidden task count is only 'about 120'. Going over fails the whole submission. The projection uses Stage 2's measured mix on dev. The fallback is 4.5 min / 28 calls (and a thinking budget of 2048).

The expected fine-tuning gain (0 to +2 tasks) is close to what 4 paired runs can resolve (SE about 0.8-1.05). A real +1 effect will usually end as NO-GO. The data comes from 4 public repos, while the hidden test repos differ (747248), so the adapter may overfit. The forum claim that 'LoRA teams dominate' (748051) is an unsupported assertion.

Train/serve mismatch: NF4 QLoRA on the bf16 QAT weights vs serving on W4A16 compressed-tensors (cos 0.998 between ct and qat). The k_eq_v duplicate fix has been verified only in source and CPU loaders until FT-0 runs. E0 measures how much of the trained delta survives serving.

Data exactness with thinking on: earlier calls are history re-renderings (a newline before <channel|>, dictsort argument order, visible content moved after the tool responses, empty thoughts dropped, forced thought ends). Each case is counted and has a labelling rule, and 'other' must be 0. Live vLLM behaviour (stop token in choices[].token_ids, return_token_ids through LiteLLM) is first checked in Stage 2.
The train-split pass rate is unknown; the yield is extrapolated from the dev histogram. The R1 >= 15 gate after pass 1 stops the track cheaply if the rate is low.

4xL4 training memory and throughput (about 120 tok/s, about 20 GB on GPU0 at 16k) are estimates. Host RAM and model-mount read speed are unknown. The Kaggle model slug capitalization and the dataset mount paths are assumptions (with a search fallback). peft and accelerate must come from a private wheels dataset because the notebook is offline.

Quota and queues: 30 quota-h is verified, but the 2x billing for 4xL4 has not been confirmed by the admins. 4xL4 queues of 3-5 h have been reported. The submission queue is about 33 h with 1 pending submission per team. Week 2 assumes the quota resets to 30, and a session that exhausts the quota is stopped.

Harness drift: the organizers changed thinking semantics, prompts and patch filtering on 10-12 without notice. Paired same-notebook evaluation protects the E comparison, but a mid-plan wheelhouse change could change the training-data format. env.json records the wheel sizes in every run; on a change, redo the Stage 2 capture checks before training.
The decision set leaves out 19 dev tasks (15 unfair, 4 never-solved fixable). If thinking-on or the adapter would solve some of them, E will not see that gain. Historically both arms score 0 on them.
In the LoRA arms, and on the scorer, the ADK summarizer also runs through the adapter, which was never trained on summarizer examples. E measures this drift together with the adapter.

The compaction interval is slightly uncertain: 15 in the current README and notebook, 5 in the 09-25 README and one participant's report. The 14,336 threshold is consistent everywhere. With thoughts kept in history, a prompt plus 8,192 output tokens can exceed 32,768 in rare cases, so overflow is checked per call.

critiques.verdict: Mostly sound; one plausible blocker to fix before Stage 6. I checked the risky correctness claims against the source and they hold: adapter key names and shapes, the k_eq_v duplicate, PEFTHelper fields, the thinking resolution on adk 0.2.13, discover_declared_models, rerouting create_model_registry through the copied config's port, the loss alignment and softcap, and the transformers 5.13.1 deps on the v170 image. Capture is exact by construction because it uses vLLM's own token ids. The blocker is the E0 parity step. It needs about 2,048 rows of full-vocab logits at once and runs before the lora1 tasks in the same notebook, so an OOM there would kill that run. Several smaller gaps would trip gates or fallbacks without breaking the plan; they are listed as non-blocking.

blocking_problems.stage: Stage 6 (E0 parity inside notebook A) / Stage 1 test (e)
blocking_problems.problem: E0 uses prompt_logprobs on the LoRA server at gmu 0.80. That needs logits for every prompt position in a prefill chunk, and it is computed on every TP rank. If it OOMs, the vLLM engine dies, and because E0 runs before any task, the lora1 dev run (about 2.6 h, 5.2 quota-h) is lost. Stage 1 test (e) as written does not catch this, because the prompt length is not specified.
blocking_problems.evidence: vLLM (wheelhouse) v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5062-5071: for each scheduled chunk it calls compute_logits(prompt_hidden_states) and then sampler.compute_logprobs, which is log_softmax in fp32 (v1/sample/sampler.py:206-207). The chunk size on L4 is the API-server default max_num_batched_tokens = 2048 (engine/arg_utils.py:2063-2068, since L4 is under 70 GiB). LogitsProcessor uses all_gather (platforms/interface.py:614-618, logits_processor.py:75-81), so each of the 4 GPUs holds [2048, 262144]: about 1.07 GB in bf16 plus 2.1 GB in fp32, plus softcap temporaries. None of this is covered by memory profiling. For comparison, forum 746503 reports an r16 all-linear adapter OOMing at gmu 0.80 on 4xL4 while 'warming up sampler with 256 dummy requests', which needs about 1/8 as many logit rows. Prefix caching is not a confound: sampling_params.py:425 skips the cache read for prompt_logprobs requests. This is a plausible failure, not one I measured.
blocking_problems.fix: (1) In Stage 1, make test (e) a token-id prompt of at least 4k tokens with prompt_logprobs=0, on the S2 (0.80) and S1 (0.90) adapter servers. Record whether it survives, and record peak memory from /metrics or nvidia-smi. (2) Move E0 out of the critical path. Either run it after the dev task loop in notebook A, wrapped so a failure cannot discard results already saved, or run it in Stage 1 or a separate short parity notebook started with extra_args ['--max-num-batched-tokens','512']. That flag is fine for a parity-only server and does not touch scorer-parity eval runs. (3) If even 512 OOMs, compute NLL from /v1/completions with echo/logprobs on shorter slices of each val sequence.

non_blocking: Stage 1 fallback probably does not address the reported failure mode. Forum 746503 shows the r16-at-0.80 failure as an OOM 'when warming up sampler with 256 dummy requests', fixed only by --max-num-seqs 8. That cost scales with max_num_seqs times the 262k vocabulary, not with LoRA rank: from findings, an r16 slot is about 0.11 GiB per GPU and r8 saves about 0.05 GiB. So S2b (r8) and S2c (attention-only) will likely fail the same way. If S2 hits that specific error, go straight to the 'pause and ask the organizers' branch instead of spending server starts on rank variants. The cause is probably unprofiled LoRA or CUDA-graph memory (cudagraph_specialize_lora=True, compilation.py:604), which no submission-side setting controls.

Stage 0 success criterion 1 cannot be met as specified. Capture wiring (1c) lives in start_model after server.start(), which is the vLLM branch. The MODEL_URL path returns before that branch (agent_eval.py:76-80), and it registers openai/gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct without install_litellm_reasoning_patch. So a mock run with CAPTURE=1 starts no proxy and writes no captures. Either also wire the proxy into the MODEL_URL branch (proxy port to MODEL_URL, with a mock that honours return_token_ids), or drop the criterion and accept that Stage 2 is the first end-to-end capture test.

Stage 4's gate 'other = 0' will likely trip on real data, from two template behaviours. (a) In the served chat_template.jinja (lines 237-240 and 260-330), an assistant message is rendered as [thought][tool_calls][tool responses][content]. Any visible text the model emitted alongside a tool call is therefore moved after the tool responses, so the located span differs from the raw C_i in more than whitespace. When content is non-empty it also appends '<turn|>
', and the next call then continues without '<|turn>model
'. (b) If the model emits an empty '<|channel>thought
<channel|>' block, the reasoning comes back as an empty string. That fails `if thinking_text` at line 239, so history drops the block entirely. Add explicit categories for 'content-reordered' and 'empty-thought-dropped', label the rendered tokens, and size the per-request fallback from Stage 2 captures rather than assuming 0.

The plan labels every history-rendered thought span. The template always writes '\n' before <channel|> (line 240), and the gemma4 reasoning parser strips the 'thought\n' label (comp/vllm/reasoning/gemma4_reasoning_parser.py:17-20, 108-116). So earlier calls in a segment train the rendered form, not the sampled bytes. Also, when thinking_token_budget forces the end of reasoning (vLLM logits_processor/builtin.py thinking_token_budget, with reasoning_config <|channel>/<channel|> from adk server.py:719-731), the forced end-of-thinking tokens become labelled targets. Consider masking a forced '<channel|>' (thought length at the budget) or dropping those calls.

Stage 5 loss NOTE is misleading. The code `idx = (labels[:,1:][0] != -100).nonzero(); hs = h[0, idx]` is already correctly aligned: h[j] predicts token j+1, which is tgt[j]. The suggested h[0, :-1][idx] is identical. A builder who 'fixes' this into h[0, idx+1] would introduce an off-by-one. Fail-fast check (i) would catch it, but the NOTE should say the code is correct as written.

Stage 2 is not a clean thinking A/B. v3b_off keeps max_output_tokens 4096 and budgets of 4.5 min / 40 calls (experiments/v3b_noedit/configs/sampling.yaml:8, eval_config.yaml). v3t_think uses 8192 and 5.0 min / 30 calls. With one run per arm this confound sits on top of the noise (SE about 1.1-1.5 tasks). The plan lists this as a risk, but the decision rule treats the difference as the effect of thinking alone.

Overflow edge with thinking ON and include_thoughts true. Compaction triggers off the previous call's prompt_token_count (threshold 14,336). In the worst case the next prompt is 14,335 + previous completion (up to 4,096 thought tokens plus the call) + one tool response (up to 5,000 chars), and vLLM rejects any request where prompt + 8,192 > 32,768. That needs a completion plus tool response over about 10.2k tokens, so it is rare but possible with long write/edit arguments or parallel calls. Stage 2's 'overflow = 0' criterion should be checked per call, not just per task outcome.

Stage 0 1(c) and the summarizer: with the adapter on the root agent, the ADK compaction summarizer also runs through openai/main_lora. Training data has no summarizer examples, so E1 measures adapter-plus-summarizer drift together. This is acceptable, but note it when interpreting results.

Unverified version pairing to fail-fast early. bitsandbytes 0.46.1 (wheelhouse) with torch 2.10.0+cu128 (image v170) has not been exercised for NF4 training. Fail-fast check (ii) covers it, but run a 2-layer NF4 forward and backward first, before the 62.6 GB load, to avoid wasting the 5-15 min load.

critiques.verdict: The plan is feasible but needs revision before it can give a trustworthy answer. I checked the quota myself: `kaggle quota` shows 30.00 GPU-hours, 0 used, refresh 2026-10-17 00:00 UTC. The 2x billing for 4xL4 is stated in docs/competition.md:132-133, so the plan's ~15 h of 4xL4 per week holds, and its arithmetic adds up (12.75 h in week 1, 13.4-14.4 h in week 2). Two problems remain. First, the budget only works if nothing has to be rerun. Second, the final GO rule cannot separate a real gain from noise. The fix is the same for both: drop the 15 "unfair" dev tasks from the decision runs. In our v3b and v3e runs they passed 0 of 75 times but took 46% of the agent time. Spend the hours saved on paired, same-server repeats. The cheapest trustworthy path is: FT-0 (0.75 h), a thinking-on calibration run on all 33 tasks, data pass 1 with an early stop on low yield, training, and E0 parity. Then make the decision with at least 4 paired LoRA-vs-control runs on the 18 core and fixable dev tasks, which costs about the same as the planned E1+E2. Also: the thinking-on prompt-only submission is the step most likely to improve the score, and nothing beyond a runtime check should hold it back.

blocking_problems.problem: The GO rule is too weak to decide anything, and the controls are pooled across different conditions. The stage text says the standard error is about 1.0-1.2 tasks with 3 runs per arm, but the design compares 3 LoRA runs with only 2 controls: the Stage 2 think run and ctl1. Those two controls also differ from each other: the Stage 2 run was in week 1 with GMU 0.90 and the capture proxy on, while ctl1 runs in week 2 with GMU 0.80, possibly on a different wheelhouse. With a per-run SD of about 1.5, the standard error of the difference is about 1.4 tasks. The +1.0 GO threshold is then only about 0.7 SE, so an adapter with no real effect passes the mean gate about 23% of the time.
blocking_problems.evidence: v3b dev scores were 11, 10 and 8 (SD 1.53; compute_eval finding, docs/experiments.md). SE = 1.53 × sqrt(1/3 + 1/2) = 1.40, and P(Z > 1.0/1.40) ≈ 0.24. The plan pools 'controls = Stage 2 think run + ctl1' (Stage 6 item 5). The organizers changed the wheelhouse without notice on 10-12 (UPDATE in the brief), so a control from another week is not like-for-like.
blocking_problems.fix: Run LoRA and control as paired variants on the same LoRA-enabled server in each notebook. Put the adapter in both variants and reference it only in the LoRA variant; agent_eval already requires an identical adapter set per server (agent_eval.py:128-137). Use at least 4 runs per arm on the 18 core and fixable tasks (see the next item; this costs about the same as the planned E1+E2). Compare per task, paired, and use either +2 tasks or a one-sided paired test as the bar. Do not pool the week-1 Stage 2 run as a control.

blocking_problems.problem: Almost half of every dev-run hour goes to the 15 dev tasks labelled 'unfair', which have never passed. They cannot change any comparison, because both arms score 0 on them. With thinking on they will mostly run until the 5-minute cap, so their share of the time grows. The plan runs all 33 dev tasks in E1 and E2: 4 runs and 10.4 h of wall time, about 70% of the week-2 quota.
blocking_problems.evidence: eval/fairness.json: core 6, fixable 12, unfair 15, with the note 'unfair ... 0 of 75 runs passed them'. My check over the v3b/v3e task_results.jsonl files in eval/runs: unfair 75 rows, 0 resolved, 10,163 s; fixable 60 rows, 16 resolved, 8,388 s; core 30 rows, 30 resolved, 1,866 s. So unfair tasks took 10,163 of 20,417 s, about 50% of agent time (about 46% of run wall time once ~6 min of startup is included).
blocking_problems.fix: For the E1/E2 decision runs (and the Stage 2 'off' arm, if it is kept), pass a splits file holding only the 18 core and fixable tasks. kaggle_build already supports --splits-file/--split. This saves about 1.2-1.3 h of wall time per thinking-on run, roughly 5 h of 4xL4 across E1+E2. Use that time for the extra paired repeats, or keep it as rerun slack. Keep Stage 2's think arm on all 33 tasks, because the 12-hour runtime projection needs the slow tasks that hit the cap.

blocking_problems.problem: The rule decides with a single run per arm, so noise alone has about a 17-20% chance of switching everything to thinking OFF. That switch would set both the training data and the deployment config. The two arms also differ in more than thinking: v3t_think uses 5.0 min / 30 calls / 8192 max output tokens, while v3b_off uses 4.5 min / 40 calls / 4096. So 'off wins by 2' would not even isolate the effect of thinking. This one noisy measurement is weighed against forum evidence that strongly favours thinking on (off 23/129 vs on 48-51/129; every public 0.17-0.18 config uses thinking on).
blocking_problems.evidence: Plan rule: 'OFF if think <= off - 2'. The SD of the difference between two single runs is 1.5 × sqrt(2) ≈ 2.1, so with equal true means P(diff ≤ -2) ≈ P(Z ≤ -0.95) ≈ 17%, or a little more after rounding to whole tasks. Budgets differ per Stage 0 items 5 and 6. Forum 746250 and the Budget-Fit config are cited in the plan's own findings (delta_evidence).
blocking_problems.fix: Keep thinking ON unless off beats think by 3 or more tasks AND a second paired run confirms it, or unless the runtime projection fails. Alternatively, drop the off arm: that saves about 1.1 h of 4xL4 wall time (2.2 quota-h), and a thinking-off control is not needed anywhere else in the plan.

blocking_problems.problem: The budget assumes nothing goes wrong. Data pass 2 is listed as conditional, but by the plan's own numbers it will almost always run. That leaves about 2.25 h of slack in week 1 and 0.6-1.6 h in week 2. No hours are set aside for the failure fallbacks the plan itself describes: rerunning a crashed notebook, re-training after an E0 parity failure, or switching to the r8 or attention-only adapter after an FT-0 failure.
blocking_problems.evidence: Pass 1 is 1 sample per task, so it can produce at most one kept trajectory per resolved task. The plan estimates '20-29 resolved per pass', which is below the gate of 40 trajectories, so pass 2 (3.0 h of wall time) will run. The budget table's note 'train in week 1 only if pass 2 is skipped' therefore describes a case that will not happen. Week 2 at 13.4-14.4 of about 15 h leaves no room for one retrain (3-4 h) or one repeated evaluation (2.6 h). 4xL4 queues of 3-5 h have also been reported (compute_eval), and unused week-1 quota is lost at the 10-17 reset.
blocking_problems.fix: Label pass 2 as expected and budget it that way. Cut the dev decision runs to the 18 core and fixable tasks (previous item) so that about 4-5 h becomes real slack. Add an explicit early stop: if pass 1 resolves fewer than 15 train tasks, stop the fine-tuning track before pass 2. That way the week-2 quota goes to evaluation only when training is likely to be worth it.

non_blocking: Quota check done (read-only `kaggle quota`, 2026-10-13): 30.00 GPU-hours total, 0.00 used, refresh 2026-10-17T00:00:00. This matches the plan's figure. The brief's '~12 h' is out of date.

The Stage 2 think-arm estimate (2.4 h) is probably optimistic. The 15 unfair and most fixable tasks took about 135-140 s each with thinking off and will mostly run to the 5.0-minute cap (+0.5 min overhead) with thinking on. A rough estimate is 15×5.5 + 12×~5 + 6×~2.5 min ≈ 2.6 h plus startup. The same bias applies to the 4.3 min/task figure for data pass 1, because the plan expects about 41 of the 72 train tasks never to pass and those will run to the cap.

The prompt-only submission gate ('think >= 10/33') is arbitrary. If thinking-on truly averages 11, a single run lands below 10 about 16% of the time. This submission has the best expected value in the whole plan (public thinking-on configs score 0.17-0.18 against our 0.12), and the ~33 h queue makes delay costly. Gate it only on: no crashes, 0 overflow errors, and a runtime projection of at most 10.5 h.

The leaderboard cannot confirm the adapter. A real dev gain of +1 to +2 out of 33 corresponds to roughly +2 to +3.5 of 58 public tasks, which is within the ±2.5 noise and the 0.06 spread seen for an identical zip. So the go/no-go decision has to come entirely from the paired dev runs. That is a further reason to make those runs as strong as possible rather than spend more on data generation.

Weigh the cost against the value. The full fine-tuning track uses about 26-27 h of 4xL4 (two weekly quotas) for an expected gain of 0 to +2 tasks. The only published trained-LoRA test was a NO-GO (2/32 vs 4/32), and no LoRA submission has been shown to score above its base. The cheap ways to stop early are FT-0 (0.75 h), the pass-1 yield, and E0 parity. Make each of them an explicit stop condition before more GPU hours are committed.

FT-0 test (e) should send a prompt of about 16k tokens, not a short one. The E0 parity check at GMU 0.80 requests prompt_logprobs over a 262k vocabulary on full-length sft_val sequences, and its extra memory at that length is unknown. If it runs out of memory, it does so at the start of the E1 LoRA notebook, before any task has run.

The control's week-to-week reproducibility is not checked anywhere. Record the pip freeze and wheelhouse file sizes in every run (the plan already suggests this), and treat any change in the wheelhouse between the two weeks as invalidating all cross-week comparisons.

findings.question: Which vLLM does the competition actually run, and is it stock?
findings.answer: vLLM 0.19.1, but a patched build. The wheelhouse copy (433,132,506 bytes) differs from the PyPI 0.19.1 wheel (433,132,101 bytes) in exactly 3 files. findings.question: Gemma 4 31B architecture (HF config, module names)
findings.answer:
Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration (model_type gemma4) with these parts:
- Text model: 60 layers, hidden 5376, MLP intermediate 21504 (gelu_pytorch_tanh, gate/up/down), 32 query heads, vocab 262144, tied embeddings, final_logit_softcapping 30, a per-layer layer_scalar. No MoE, no per-layer inputs (hidden_size_per_layer_input 0), no KV sharing (num_kv_shared_layers 0).
- Sliding layers (50): head_dim 256, 16 KV heads, window 1024, rope theta 10k.
- Full-attention layers (10, indices 5,11,17,...,59): head_dim 512, 4 KV heads (num_global_key_value_heads), attention_k_eq_v=true. These layers have NO v_proj: HF computes value_states = k_proj(x), then v_norm. Rotary is partial (0.25, theta 1e6).
- Vision tower: 27 layers, hidden 1152. Its linears are Gemma4ClippableLinear wrappers whose real nn.Linear is named `.linear`. There is also model.embed_vision.embedding_projection. No audio tower (audio_config null).
- HF module paths: model.language_model.layers.N.self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj and model.language_model.layers.N.mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj.
- Projection shapes (in->out):
  - Sliding: q 5376->8192, k/v 5376->4096, o 8192->5376.
  - Global: q 5376->16384, k 5376->2048, o 16384->5376.
  - MLP: gate/up 5376->21504, down 21504->5376.
- The QAT-unquantized index has 60 k_proj but only 50 v_proj. The ct config text_config is identical to the QAT-unquantized one apart from duplicated top-level fields.
findings.evidence: Configs downloaded via kagglehub into ft_research/cfg/{ct,qatu,bf16}/config.json. Index analysis of cfg/qatu/model.safetensors.index.json: 1188 keys, `self_attn.v_proj.weight` x50. transformers 5.13.1 modeling_gemma4.py:1195 (use_alternative_attention), 1225-1229 (v_proj None), 1264 (V = key_states). ct safetensors header (range-read): layers.0.k_proj weight_packed [4096,672].

findings.question: Which modules can vLLM apply LoRA to on this model, and how are PEFT names mapped?
findings.answer:
Supported LoRA targets are the LinearBase layers of the language model: packed qkv_proj (from q_proj/k_proj/v_proj), o_proj, packed gate_up_proj (from gate_proj/up_proj), and down_proj.
- The adapter loader's expected-suffix set is {q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj,embedding_projection}.
- embedding_modules is empty, so LoRA on embed_tokens/lm_head is not supported.
- The vision tower is an HF AutoModel with plain nn.Linear (not LinearBase), so it is not supported. A vision key such as `...q_proj.linear.lora_A.weight` gives suffix `linear`, which raises ValueError in check_unexpected_modules. With static --lora-modules that aborts server startup (serving.py:130-131).
- Tower/connector LoRA is off (enable_tower_connector_lora=False), so embed_vision LoRA would be ignored.
- Name mapping: parse_fine_tuned_lora_name strips `base_model.model.` and applies hf_to_vllm_mapper prefixes. `model.language_model.` becomes `language_model.model.`, and a bare `model` prefix becomes `language_model.model`. So both conditional-gen keys (base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N...) and text-only CausalLM keys (base_model.model.model.layers.N...) resolve to language_model.model.layers.N.... Both pass.
- Adapter-config fields vLLM reads (PEFTHelper): r, lora_alpha, target_modules (required to exist; its content is NOT used for matching), bias (must be 'none'), modules_to_save (must be null), use_dora (must be false), use_rslora.
- Ignored: base_model_name_or_path, task_type, rank_pattern, alpha_pattern. One global scaling alpha/r is used, so do not use rank_pattern/alpha_pattern.

findings.question: Does LoRA work on compressed-tensors W4A16 (Marlin) layers? Any restrictions with TP=4?
findings.answer:
Yes.
- BaseLinearLayerWithLoRA.apply runs base_layer.quant_method.apply (Marlin W4A16) and then adds the punica LoRA delta in lora_dtype. 'auto' means the model dtype, bf16. _get_lora_device and .weight explicitly handle `weight_packed` (compressed-tensors).
- TP=4: QKV/MergedColumn LoRA slice lora_b per shard, and RowParallel slices lora_a.
- Global layers have 4 KV heads, so 1 per GPU and no replication.
- fully_sharded_loras defaults to False.
- I found no TP-specific LoRA restriction.
- cudagraph_specialize_lora defaults to True, so separate CUDA graphs are captured with and without LoRA. That costs extra startup time and memory; magnitude unknown.
findings.evidence: comp/vllm/lora/layers/base_linear.py:21-31, 137-160, 162-176. lora/layers/utils.py:32-54. lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py:356-411 (MergedQKVParallelLinearWithLoRA output_slices from per-layer num_kv_heads/head_size). row_parallel_linear.py:27 (input_size_per_partition). config/compilation.py:604 (cudagraph_specialize_lora True).

findings.question: Train/serve mismatch on the 10 k_eq_v (full-attention) layers
findings.answer:
Mismatch confirmed.
- At load time vLLM copies the k_proj base weights into the V slot of qkv_proj (gemma4.py:1649-1658).
- The LoRA for that V slot comes only from a `...layers.L.self_attn.v_proj` entry, and PEFT never produces one for L in {5,11,...,59}. So _create_merged_loras_inplace packs [q, k, None].
- In vLLM, K gets the k_proj LoRA delta but V does not. In HF/PEFT training, V = k_proj(x) including the delta.
- There is no Gemma4-specific LoRA handling in vLLM.
- Fix (recommended): duplicate each global-layer k_proj lora_A/lora_B as v_proj (20 extra tensors, about 0.5% of size). vLLM then computes V = (W_k + s·B_k·A_k)x, exactly as HF does. Alternative: do not target k_proj on those 10 layers.
- Verified with the replicated loader logic that the duplicated keys pass vLLM's checks.
findings.evidence: lora/model_manager.py:632-668 (merge with None slices), lora_weights.py:127-139 (pack handles None). grep shows no 'lora' handling in gemma4.py beyond SupportsLoRA. Tiny test: ft_research/fix_k_eq_v.py on ft_research/tiny/fixtest gives validate_adapter.py PASS with no warning. Without the fix the validator warns 'k_proj LoRA without v_proj'.

findings.question: adk_submission 0.2.12 adapter handling (discovery.py, server.py)
findings.answer:
How adapters are discovered and served:
- **Discovery:** every *.safetensors under adapters/ is collected (swegemma restricts adapter extensions to .safetensors). Files in a dir that has adapter_config.json, or named adapter_model*, are grouped into one adapter named by the relative dir path with '/' replaced by '_'. So adapters/main_lora/{adapter_config.json,adapter_model.safetensors} becomes 'main_lora'. The name must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$.
- **Stray files:** a stray .safetensors outside a PEFT dir becomes its own 'adapter' and would break vLLM startup.
- **Rank:** taken from adapter_config.json 'r'. If that is missing, it is the max over lora_A/B tensors of min(shape).
- **Server (VllmServer.build_cmd):** if enable_lora and any adapters exist, it passes --enable-lora and --max-loras = NUMBER OF MOUNTED ADAPTERS, not 1 and not config.max_loras=8. It also passes --max-lora-rank = smallest bucket in (1,8,16,32,64,128,256,320,512) that is >= max r; config.max_lora_rank=128 is used only if some rank is unknown. Then --lora-modules name=dir ...
- **Memory:** gpu_memory_utilization and max_model_len do NOT change when adapters exist. LoRA buffers are allocated at model load, before KV profiling, so they come straight out of the KV cache.
- **Merge path:** TransformersServer._merge_lora_if_needed (PeftModel merge_and_unload, server.py:526-603) runs only with backend='transformers' and supports one adapter. swegemma's registry defaults backend='vllm' (registry.py:76). The README and the organizer notebook use VllmServer, and peft is not in the wheelhouse. So the scorer uses vLLM multi-LoRA, and the model id is openai/<adapter_name>.

findings.question: QAT: is w4a16-ct quantized from qat-q4_0-unquantized, and will an adapter trained on the unquantized QAT weights transfer?
findings.answer:
Yes, ct is derived from the QAT checkpoint, but the re-quantization is lossy.
- The ct README front-matter says base_model: google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized.
- ct quantization_config: compressed-tensors pack-quantized, int4 symmetric, group_size 32, observer memoryless_minmax, version 0.15.1.a20260521. Ignored (not quantized): the vision tower, embed_vision.embedding_projection and lm_head.
- I range-read real tensors from both Kaggle checkpoints (layers.0 k_proj, layers.5 o_proj, layers.30 up_proj). The QAT weights sit on a 16-level Q4_0-style grid per 32-element group (step about absmax/8, at most 16 distinct values per group).
- The ct checkpoint re-quantized them with scale = absmax/7.5 (exactly: 100% of scales match). q_ct == round(W_qat/scale_ct) for 98.8% of entries. So ct is round-to-nearest of the QAT weights onto a mismatched grid, not a lossless repack.
- Measured on layer0 k_proj:
  - mean|ct-qat| = 0.00072, about 6.7% of mean|W|; cos(ct, qat) = 0.9982.
  - cos(ct, bf16 base) = 0.9935; cos(qat, bf16 base) = 0.9956; mean|qat-bf16| = 0.00258, about 19%.
- Conclusion: the QAT-unquantized bf16 checkpoint is by far the closest bf16 proxy to what is served. An adapter trained on it should transfer, and much better than one trained on gemma-4-31b-it bf16. Whether the small residual gap matters for task score is unknown.
- Exact match is possible: dequantize ct (q·scale) to bf16 and train on that. The decode was verified, but dequant_ct.py itself has not been run end-to-end.
- Note: compressed_tensors 0.15 removed CompressedLinear (`from_linear` raises), so training directly on the compressed model in HF needs run_compressed=False (decompression to bf16, about 62 GB). Untested.

adapter_compat.recommended_settings:
Layout: adapters/<name>/adapter_config.json + adapters/<name>/adapter_model.safetensors (bf16). Put nothing else under adapters/. Do not ship tokenizer files. agent.yaml uses `adapter: <name>`.

adapter_config.json (what vLLM accepts and uses):
{
  "peft_type": "LORA",
  "task_type": "CAUSAL_LM",                                   // ignored by vLLM
  "base_model_name_or_path": "google/gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct", // ignored by vLLM and harness; any string
  "r": 16,                    // <=128; vLLM --max-lora-rank = bucket(r) from {8,16,32,64,128}
  "lora_alpha": 32,           // scaling = alpha/r (or alpha/sqrt(r) if use_rslora)
  "lora_dropout": 0.0,
  "bias": "none",             // required
  "use_dora": false,          // required
  "use_rslora": false,
  "modules_to_save": null,    // required
  "target_modules": ".*language_model.*\\.(q_proj|k_proj|v_proj|o_proj|gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj)",
  "rank_pattern": {}, "alpha_pattern": {}   // must stay empty (vLLM ignores them, which would give wrong scaling)
}
PEFT training: use exactly that regex string for target_modules, or train a text-only Gemma4ForCausalLM with the 7-name list. Do NOT use the plain 7-name list on Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration (PEFT raises on the vision Gemma4ClippableLinear). Do NOT use 'all-linear' (adds vision `.linear` keys, so vLLM startup fails). Do not target embed_tokens/lm_head.

Safetensors keys vLLM accepts (either style works):
  base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.{0..59}.self_attn.{q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj}.lora_{A,B}.weight
  base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.{0..59}.mlp.{gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj}.lora_{A,B}.weight
  (text-only style base_model.model.model.layers.N... also maps correctly)
Shapes: lora_A [r, in], lora_B [out, r].
- Sliding layers: q 5376->8192, k/v 5376->4096, o 8192->5376.
- Global layers 5,11,...,59: q 5376->16384, k 5376->2048, o 16384->5376.
- MLP: 5376<->21504.

Required post-processing (k_eq_v fix): for L in range(5,60,6), copy layers.L.self_attn.k_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight to layers.L.self_attn.v_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight (cloned tensors). Script: ft_research/fix_k_eq_v.py. Then run ft_research/validate_adapter.py <dir> --real (replicates vLLM's PEFTHelper, name mapper and unexpected-module check, plus 31B shape checks).

Base weights for training: gemma-4-31b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized (bf16, closest proxy). For an exact match, dequantize ct with ft_research/dequant_ct.py and use the qatu config.json without quantization_config.

Testing anywhere off-Kaggle: pip install the wheelhouse vllm-0.19.1 wheel (v23+, 433,132,506 bytes), not PyPI's.

Scratch artefacts (all under ft_research/):
- cfg/{ct,qatu,bf16}/config.json, README.md and index files
- comp/vllm/ (patched source)
- src/ (PyPI vllm, transformers 5.13.1, peft 0.21.2, compressed_tensors)
- tiny/ (PEFT key-name experiments)
- rangefetch.py
risks: Any adapter key outside the language model (vision `.linear`, embed_vision, lm_head/embed_tokens), or a stray .safetensors under adapters/, makes vLLM raise during init_static_loras. The server never starts and the submission errors. Validate before submitting.

k_eq_v mismatch: without duplicating k_proj LoRA into v_proj on layers 5,11,...,59, vLLM applies the k delta to K but not V. HF training applied it to both, so the served model differs from the trained one on 10 of 60 layers.

Stock PyPI vllm 0.19.1 cannot serve LoRA on this model at all, and wheelhouse versions before v23 silently zero adapters. Off-Kaggle tests (Lightning) must use the current wheelhouse wheel. No GPU measurement in this session confirms that an adapter changes outputs on the current scorer.

ct is a lossy round-to-nearest re-quantization of the QAT weights (scale absmax/7.5 vs the QAT grid of about absmax/8; cos 0.998). Training on qat-unquantized is close but not identical to what is served, and the impact on task score is unknown. QLoRA (NF4) adds another, different quantization error on top.
rank_pattern/alpha_pattern and per-module ranks are ignored by vLLM (one alpha/r scaling), so outputs would be silently mis-scaled.

Memory figures are computed from source, not measured. cudagraph_specialize_lora=True adds extra CUDA-graph captures (startup time and memory, unknown size). Every discovered adapter counts toward --max-loras and buffer memory even if no agent references it.

The scorer's scripts/inference.py is not available. That it uses VllmServer.build_cmd (with its adapter-count and rank-bucket override) is inferred from HARNESS_README section 3 and the organizer notebook. Whether the 8-adapter limit is enforced is unknown; no harness code enforces it.

findings.question: (2b) Should Gemma 4 training use eager or sdpa attention, and are there other training gotchas?
findings.answer: Use sdpa. Global layers have head_dim 512 (global_head_dim), so flash_attention_2 cannot be used model-wide: FA2 supports head_dim up to 256, and Unsloth's source says so for this exact model. Eager materializes [32, S, S] fp32 scores, about 34 GB per layer at 16k, so it cannot work for long sequences. PyTorch SDPA's mem-efficient backend has no head_dim upper bound on CUDA, so it handles 512 and the masked sliding layers. It does compute the full S×S tile set for the explicit sliding-window mask (O(S²) work although the window is 1024). Unsloth ships a banded O(S·w) kernel for exactly this. Other gotchas: (a) final_logit_softcapping=30 is applied in forward; attention has no softcap (scaling=1.0, with q/k/v RMSNorm). With a 262,144 vocab, full logits are 16k×262k bf16 = 8.6 GB per copy, and the softcap div/tanh/mul plus the fp32 upcast in the loss make several copies, so naive HF loss OOMs on L4 above ~2-4k tokens. Use a chunked loss on labeled positions only, or Liger FLCE. (b) Use bf16. Unsloth force-upcasts Gemma 4 in fp16 because fp16 gives NaN grad norms in backward, and the L4 (sm89) supports bf16. (c) Text-only input needs no token_type_ids or mm_token_type_ids. The bidirectional mask applies only to vision tokens ('use_bidirectional_attention': 'vision'); without mm_token_type_ids the model uses standard causal and sliding masks. (d) The sliding window is 1024 on 50 layers; 10 global layers use partial rotary 0.25 and rope_theta 1e6. Nothing needs configuring. (e) transformers 5.13.1 DynamicCache builds zero layers when num_kv_shared_layers==0 (cache_utils.py:1565-1566, `layer_types[:-0]`), so HF generate with use_cache likely raises IndexError on 31B. Train with use_cache=False and evaluate with vLLM. (f) The tokenizer has padding_side 'left' and the template already emits <bos>: tokenize rendered text with add_special_tokens=False and right-pad (or use bs=1). (g) Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration sets accepts_loss_kwargs=False, so Trainer averages loss per micro-batch, not per token, across grad accumulation. (h) The chat template has no {% generation %} tags, so TRL assistant_only_loss will not work and you need your own mask. Tool calls and tool responses sit inside one model turn: '<|turn>model\n<|tool_call>call:NAME{…}<tool_call|><|tool_response>response:NAME{…}<tool_response|>…'. Generation stops on eos ids [1, 106 (<turn|>), 50 (<|tool_response>)]. Train labels on model-written spans, including the closing <tool_call|> and the following <|tool_response> stop token (id 50) or <turn|> (106), and mask the tool-response body. The served kwargs are enable_thinking=True, which adds '<|think|>' to the system turn. Render training text with the exact kwargs and tool list used at inference.

VERSIONS
Kaggle training notebook, internet ON:
pip install "transformers==5.13.1" "peft==0.21.2" "accelerate==1.15.0" "bitsandbytes==0.46.1" "safetensors>=0.8.0" ["liger-kernel==0.8.4"] ["trl==1.14.1"]
The image already has torch 2.10.0+cu128, datasets 5.0.0 and Python 3.12.

Offline alternative: from /kaggle/input/datasets/metric/gemma-4-developer-agent-wheelhouse run

and use the image's peft 0.19.1 and accelerate 1.13.0.

Lightning A100/H100: the same pins, on torch 2.10.

LOADING (HF stack)

```python
import torch, re
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
P = "/kaggle/input/models/google/gemma-4/transformers/gemma-4-31b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized/2"
bnb = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
        bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(P, quantization_config=bnb, dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        attn_implementation="sdpa", device_map="auto",   # single 80GB GPU: device_map={"":0}
        max_memory={0:"16GiB",1:"21GiB",2:"21GiB",3:"21GiB"})   # this is Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration
model.config.use_cache = False
for p in model.parameters(): p.requires_grad_(False)
model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})
# NOT prepare_model_for_kbit_training (it upcasts the 1.4B embedding to fp32)
TARGET = (r"model\.language_model\.layers\.\d+\.(self_attn\.(q_proj|v_proj|o_proj)|mlp\.(gate_proj|up_proj|down_proj))"
          r"|model\.language_model\.layers\.(?!(?:5|11|17|23|29|35|41|47|53|59)\.)\d+\.self_attn\.k_proj")
lcfg = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.0, bias="none", target_modules=TARGET,
                  task_type="CAUSAL_LM", use_dora=False, use_rslora=False)
model = get_peft_model(model, lcfg)   # expect 400 modules, 121.2M trainable params
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(P); tok.padding_side = "right"
```
The regex keeps k_proj off the 10 k_eq_v global layers, because vLLM would not apply that LoRA to V. Fallback if FT-0 shows vLLM instability: attention only (q, v, o).

LOSS (device-safe, softcapped, only on labeled positions, chunked)
```python
def lm_loss(model, input_ids, labels, chunk=1024):
    base = model.get_base_model()
    h = base.model(input_ids=input_ids, use_cache=False).last_hidden_state   # [1,S,5376]
    tgt = labels[:, 1:]; idx = (tgt[0] != -100).nonzero().squeeze(-1)
    W = base.lm_head.weight; hs = h[0, idx].to(W.device); y = tgt[0, idx].to(W.device)
    def ce(hc, yc):
        z = torch.tanh((hc @ W.T).float() / 30.0) * 30.0
        return torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(z, yc, reduction="sum")
    tot = sum(torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(ce, hs[i:i+chunk], y[i:i+chunk], use_reentrant=False)
              for i in range(0, len(y), chunk))
    return tot / max(len(y), 1)
```
Labels: the model-written tokens of each model turn, i.e. thought/content, '<|tool_call>…<tool_call|>', plus the following stop token: id 50 '<|tool_response>' or id 106 '<turn|>'. Set -100 everywhere else, including tool-response bodies, the system prompt and the tools block. Render text with the same chat template, tools and enable_thinking=True as served, and tokenize with add_special_tokens=False.

HYPERPARAMETERS
Rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0. AdamW (torch fused), lr 1e-4 (try 2e-4 if the loss barely moves), cosine schedule with warmup 5% (min 3 steps), weight_decay 0, max_grad_norm 1.0, bf16, batch 1 sequence with grad accumulation 8, at most 2 epochs (about 20 optimizer steps per epoch for about 170 segments), max_len 16384 (20480 on an 80 GB GPU), seed fixed. Save with model.save_pretrained(out, safe_serialization=True) after casting the LoRA weights to bf16. Expect about 243 MB and 800 tensors named base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.{self_attn,mlp}.X_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight. Assert that no key contains 'vision', and keep adapter_config r=16 with use_dora=false.

BUDGET (estimates)
- 4x L4 naive MP at 16k: about 120 tok/s, about 140 s per sequence, peak about 20 GB on GPU0. 1.7M tokens per epoch ≈ 4 h, so 2 epochs ≈ 8 h of 4x L4 wall time (it bills at double the GPU rate).
- Single A100 80GB: about 380 tok/s, about 75 min per epoch, about 39 GB at 16k.
- Single H100 80GB: about 1000 tok/s, about 30 min per epoch.
- Recommendation: train on a Lightning.ai A100/H100 if available. Spend the Kaggle hours on data generation (4x72 train-task runs ≈ 9-10 h of 4x L4) and the FT-0 vLLM adapter check.

risks: Train/serve mismatch from quantization: training uses NF4 (blocksize 64, non-uniform grid) on the QAT bf16 weights, while serving uses compressed-tensors int4 symmetric group-32 (W4A16). The LoRA partly learns NF4-specific corrections. This is standard QLoRA practice and is probably small, but it is unmeasured. Check the adapter's effect in vLLM on held-out trajectories (FT-0).

k_eq_v global layers: a k_proj LoRA in layers 5, 11, …, 59 would change V in HF training but not in vLLM, because vLLM loads the base K weights into the V slot and applies no LoRA there. Exclude those modules (regex given).

The vLLM LoRA path for Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration exists only through the wheelhouse's local patch. Prior reports say rank 32 on all layers was unstable and that LoRA once shrank the KV cache to about 7.6k. Run FT-0 (load the adapter in the exact scorer vLLM config, check KV size and that the outputs change) before any training spend.

Naive HF loss materializes 262k-vocab logits (8.6 GB per bf16 copy at 16k, several copies with softcap and fp32) and will OOM on L4. A chunked loss or Liger is mandatory. Liger's Gemma4 forward probably fails across devices under device_map model parallel.

flash_attention_2 cannot be used (head_dim 512 on global layers), and eager OOMs at long context. SDPA mem-efficient computes the full S² for sliding layers, so throughput is lower than the parameter count suggests. All tokens/s figures are estimates, not measurements.

transformers 5.13.1 DynamicCache bug for num_kv_shared_layers==0 (cache_utils.py:1565-1566): HF generate with a cache on the 31B model probably crashes. Train with use_cache=False and do sanity generation in vLLM.

The Kaggle image ships transformers 5.0.0 (no Gemma 4) and lacks bitsandbytes and trl. Forgetting the upgrade gives 'model type gemma4 not recognized'. Installing Unsloth would downgrade transformers to 5.5.0, trl to 0.24.0 and datasets to below 4.4, which conflicts with the harness's 5.13.1. Keep separate environments.

Data formatting is the largest correctness risk. Gemma 4's template keeps tool calls and responses inside one model turn, strips earlier thinking, and needs enable_thinking=True plus the exact tools list as served. Masks must include the stop token (<|tool_response> id 50 or <turn|> id 106). Compaction breaks prefix continuity, so split at each compaction.

Host RAM and model-mount read speed on the Kaggle 4xL4 machine are unknown. Loading and quantizing 62.6 GB of bf16 could be slow; consider saving the NF4 model once.

findings.question: (1) Where should we intercept to get a faithful training example: the harness ATIF traces, ADK callbacks/plugins, or a logging proxy between LiteLLM and vLLM?
findings.answer: Use a logging reverse proxy between LiteLLM and vLLM, and have it add "return_token_ids": true to every request. vLLM then returns the exact prompt_token_ids it rendered and the exact token_ids the model sampled. The ATIF traces cannot produce faithful examples, for six reasons. (a) The system prompt is wrong: the trace records agent.instruction only, but ADK appends 'You are an agent. Your internal name is "swe_coder". The description about you is "..."' after it (the instructions processor runs before identity, joined with a blank line). (b) Tool schemas are not recorded. (c) Compaction is invisible: the 99 v3b dev traces contain 0 compaction entries, yet 52 of them show the prompt dropping from about 14.5k tokens to 3.6-7.9k. The compaction event is appended straight to the session and never reaches the trace callback, so the summary message the model saw afterwards is missing. (d) Tool results are re-encoded with json.dumps(default=str), which uses ensure_ascii=True, while LiteLLM sends ensure_ascii=False. Every non-ASCII character (rich's box-drawing output, emoji in issues) would be wrong. (e) Text is .strip()ed and tool_call ids are renumbered (call_2, call_4...). (f) Template-level details are invisible. An ADK plugin's before_model_callback only sees the genai LlmRequest before LiteLLM converts it and vLLM renders it, so it has the same problem of not showing the exact tokens. It would need monkeypatching into the harness's App plugins list, and it does not see summarizer calls. An in-process patch of LiteLLMClient.acompletion would work for request JSON, but LiteLLM may drop vLLM's extra token-id fields when it parses the response (unverified). The proxy sees the raw HTTP and is the simplest exact source.

findings.question: What exactly does the model receive per request? (system prompt, tools, tool results, compaction, summarizer calls)
findings.answer:
Verified body from LiteLLM, captured with a mock server. It contains messages [system, user task prompt, assistant{tool_calls:[{id, function:{name, arguments: JSON string}}]} with no content key, {role:'tool', tool_call_id, content: JSON string of the tool's dict}], tools (OpenAI function schemas; Optional fields flattened to {type, nullable:true} by the adk_submission patch), temperature, top_p, top_k sent as 64.0 (not dropped despite drop_params), max_completion_tokens 4096, and chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking:false}. The model string is 'openai//kaggle/input/models/google/gemma-4/other/...'. Because it contains 'gemma-4' and not 'gemma4', the tool role is 'tool', not 'tool_responses'. vLLM 0.19.1 detects the Kaggle template's content format as 'openai'. Strings are wrapped into [{type:text}] parts and tool-call arguments are json.loads'ed into dicts. Rendered with the served chat_template.jinja, a request looks like this: '<bos><|turn>system
SYS <|tool>declaration:...<tool|><turn|>
<|turn>user
TASK<turn|>
<|turn>model
<|channel>thought
<channel|>'. Note the trailing space after the system text, which comes from the openai-format path, and the empty thought block that only appears in the generation prompt. All later calls within the same turn render as one continuing model turn: '<|tool_call>call:run_command{command:<|"|>ls<|"|>}<tool_call|><|tool_response>response:run_command{value:<|"|>{"status": "ok", ...}<|"|>}<tool_response|>'. There is no generation prefix after it, so the model continues right after <tool_response|>. Tool results therefore appear as a JSON string inside value:<|"|>...<|"|>. Stop tokens are generation_config eos [1 <eos>, 106 <turn|>, 50 <|tool_response>]. A tool call ends by sampling <|tool_response> (50), and a final answer ends with <turn|> (106). Compaction runs as a request processor before each model call, once the last prompt_token_count reaches 14336. It keeps the last 5 events and summarizes the rest, including the original task prompt. The summarizer is a separate request with no system message, no tools and no sampling params: one user message starting 'The following is a conversation history between a user and an AI agent...', containing only text parts, so tool calls and results are dropped. The summary event has author 'model', which is not 'swe_coder', so it reaches the agent as a user message with parts ['For context:', '[model] said: <summary>']. These render as 'For context:[model] said: ...' (parts trimmed and concatenated with no separator).

findings.question: (2) How should a multi-turn trajectory (with compaction) become training examples, and how should loss be masked?
findings.answer:
Use one example per compaction segment, built only from vLLM token ids. A segment is a maximal run of agent requests where each request's messages list extends the previous one by appending. Compaction, which replaces history, starts a new segment, and retries of the same prompt are collapsed. Sequence = P_last + C_last. Each earlier completion C_i is located inside P_last: P_i, minus a trailing empty-thought block, is a prefix of P_last, and the tokens after it up to and including the next stop token (50 or 106) are C_i's history rendering. Loss goes only on those spans and on C_last: each tool call '<|tool_call>...<tool_call|><|tool_response>' and the final answer '...<turn|>'. Everything else gets label -100: system, tool declarations, user/task/nudge/'For context' summary messages, tool responses, the '
' after <turn|>, and assistant turns that were kept from before a compaction (they were already trained in the earlier segment). Two exactness details. (a) The first call after a user turn was generated after '<|turn>model
<|channel>thought
<channel|>', but history renders omit that block. The converter re-inserts it, masked, so that call sees exactly its prompt; later calls in that turn then see 4 extra context tokens. (b) History re-renders tool-call arguments with dictsort. In my synthetic test, a raw read_file{filepath,start_line,end_line} becomes {end_line,filepath,start_line}, so for multi-argument calls the labelled span may differ from the raw sample. The converter counts exact versus re-rendered spans; single-argument run_command calls are identical. Per-request examples would be exact for every call but cost far more tokens. Resolved v3b dev trajectories average 17.5 calls, a final prompt of 10.0k tokens, a summed prompt of 147k tokens and 2.3k completion tokens. Segments: about 11-13k tokens per trajectory. Per-request: about 147k tokens per trajectory, roughly 11x more. Use per-request examples only as a fallback for segments the stitcher cannot locate.
