Token statistics come from 29 resolved and 70 failed v3b dev traces (3 runs); 6 of the 29 resolved hit compaction (fastapi_14616 three times, fastapi_14873 and fastapi_15589).

findings.question: Does vLLM 0.19.1 return exact prompt and completion token ids in a non-streaming chat completion?
findings.answer: Yes, when the request sets return_token_ids: true. The response then carries top-level prompt_token_ids and choices[i].token_ids. ADK always calls with stream=False because the harness RunConfig uses the default streaming mode. The scheduler appends the stop token before checking for a stop, so the stop token should be in the output token ids; that this reaches choices[].token_ids is not verified on a live server. The converter appends 50 or 106 if it is missing (unless finish_reason is 'length').

findings.question: (3) Task-level filtering and yield: how many runs per train task (K) are needed for about 50-100 good trajectories?
findings.answer: Filters: (1) resolved==True in runs/<v>/results/task_results.jsonl, and error is empty. (2) submit_patch was called and a final text answer exists. (3) No continuation nudge: a user message after the first that does not start with 'For context:'. (4) No finish_reason 'length' and no completion whose content contains '<|tool_call>' without a parsed call (garbled). (5) No tool result containing 'mandatory input parameters are not present', and no LiteLLM placeholder for a missing tool result. (6) At most 2 exact repeats of the previous call (name and arguments); mask repeated spans, or drop the trajectory above 2. (7) The patch touches only library source: no tests/, no repro*.py or other stray files. (8) Dedupe: identical C-token sequences, then the same normalized patch for a task (keep the shorter trajectory). (9) Cap of 3 trajectories per task (prefer fewer calls and distinct patches) so that always-pass tasks do not dominate. (10) Never use dev tasks, including the 29 resolved dev traces, which are not exact anyway. Yield: the train split has 72 tasks (fastapi 41, rich 28, requests 3), the older tasks per repo. The only pass-rate evidence is dev: over 6 post-fix runs, 6 of 33 tasks passed every run, 3 passed 3-5 times, 4 passed once and 19 never (mean 9.5/33). Scaled to 72 tasks: about 13 near-always, 9 frequent (~65%), 9 rare (~17%) and 41 never, so about 20 resolved per pass. With a cap of 3 per task: K=3 gives about 60 raw and about 58 kept; K=4 about 80 raw and about 67 kept; K=6 about 120 raw and about 74 kept (about 90 with a cap of 4). About 22-25 distinct tasks contribute. The actual train pass rate is unknown: older tasks may be more contaminated (easier) or behave differently, so measure after pass 1. Cost: a dev pass of 33 tasks took about 1.07 h including about 6 min of vLLM start, about 1.75 min per task, so one train pass of 72 tasks is about 2.1 h. Adaptive plan: 2 full passes (2 notebooks in parallel, about 2.3 h each), then 2-3 extra passes only on tasks with at least one pass and fewer than 3 kept (about 15-20 tasks, about 0.6 h per pass). That totals about 6-7 GPU-hours for about 60-70 trajectories and leaves about 5 h of the 12 for FT-0/eval. Labelled tokens will be small, about 2.3k per trajectory, so about 140-160k in total.

findings.question: (4) Proxy implementation, file layout and conversion outline
findings.answer: Proxy (written and tested): scratch dp/capture_proxy.py. It uses only the standard library (ThreadingHTTPServer + http.client, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, 1800 s upstream timeout) and runs as a daemon thread in the notebook. It forwards everything. For non-streaming /v1/chat/completions it adds return_token_ids and strips prompt_token_ids and choices[].token_ids from the response before returning it, so the agent sees an unchanged response. It labels each record kind=agent (has tools), summarizer (matches the ADK summarizer prompt) or other, and appends one JSON line to captures/<variant>/<instance_id>.jsonl.gz (gzip append; multi-member files read back fine). Record fields: seq, t_start, t_end, variant, instance_id, kind, http_status, first_user_sha1, request (exact LiteLLM body), response (exact vLLM body minus token ids), prompt_token_ids, completion_token_ids. Tested end to end with ADK LiteLlm through the proxy to a mock vLLM, with 4 sequential calls on keep-alive: the agent received the parsed tool call and the capture held the token ids. Size: about 25-100 KB per request (gzip vs raw) × about 1800 requests per 72-task pass, so roughly 45-180 MB per pass. Converter: scratch dp/convert_captures.py. Join captures with task_results.jsonl and patches/, apply the filters, then agent_requests, then split_segments, then build_example, and write sft.jsonl lines {input_ids, labels, meta:{variant, instance_id, segment_idx, calls, exact, rerendered, unlocated, n_tokens}}. Also verify on the first real capture that each request's messages render, with the Kaggle template and openai-format normalization, to exactly its prompt_token_ids, and log any mismatch.

findings.question: Is Kaggle's vLLM 0.19.1 the same as the PyPI release? Does a LoRA actually get applied?
findings.answer: No, it is not the same. The wheelhouse vLLM wheel differs from PyPI 0.19.1 in three files. gemma4_mm.py adds SupportsLoRA to Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration; stock 0.19.1 raises 'does not support LoRA yet'. gemma4.py stores the shared decoder_layers and embedding modules through __dict__, so they are not registered twice. lora/model_manager.py skips reset_lora for module objects that were already loaded and skips BaseLayerWithLoRA. Together these fix the bug where 'adapters are silently wiped' (topic 743508, fixed in wheelhouse v23). Consequence: serving LoRA anywhere else (Lightning) requires this exact wheel from the Kaggle dataset, with torch==2.10.0. Nobody on the forum has yet confirmed an adapter taking effect in a scored run (topic 745364, 2026-10-03, no replies).
findings.evidence: The two RECORD files differ only in vllm/lora/model_manager.py, models/gemma4.py and models/gemma4_mm.py (sha256 of Kaggle wheel 71a87f46..., PyPI 6b29fdc2...). Diffs are in scratchpad/ft_research/my/{kag,pyp}. The vLLM METADATA requires torch==2.10.0 and compressed-tensors==0.15.0.1. Admin, 743508 (2026-09-30): 'The zeroing fix landed in v23 of the wheelhouse'.

findings.question: What are the correct adapter key names and shapes, computed without the 62 GB base model?
findings.answer: Keys: base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight and ...layers.N.mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj.lora_{A,B}.weight. lora_A has shape [r, in] and lora_B [out, r]. The patched gemma4_mm mapper rewrites model.language_model. to language_model.model.; text-only keys of the form model.layers.N also map correctly through the 'model' prefix rule. Dims: hidden 5376, intermediate 21504, 60 layers. Layers 5, 11, ..., 59 use full attention: q has 32x512 = 16384 outputs, k has 4x512 = 2048, there is NO v_proj (attention_k_eq_v), and o maps 16384 to 5376. The other 50 layers use sliding attention: q 8192, k 4096, v 4096, o 8192 to 5376. All seven target modules give r16 = 234 MiB (122M params) and r64 = 934 MiB; HARNESS_README's 110–220 MB is low. Train/serve mismatch: in HF Gemma4, the V of a full-attention layer is the pre-norm output of k_proj, so a k_proj LoRA also changes V. In vLLM, K is copied into the V slot of the packed qkv_proj, but the LoRA delta only reaches the K slice. Fix options: export the k_proj LoRA again as v_proj on the 10 global layers (supported via --dup-k-as-v), or leave k_proj out on those layers.
findings.evidence: The served model's config.json text_config and quantization_config (all language Linear layers int4 group-32; only lm_head is ignored). Header of the served safetensors: layers.0 q_proj.weight_packed [8192,672]; layers.5 q [16384,672], k [2048,672], no v_proj. HF index of google/gemma-4-31B-it: layer 5 has no v_proj. transformers 5.13.1 modeling_gemma4.py:1225-1271 has 'value_states = ... if self.v_proj is not None else key_states'. vLLM gemma4.py:296-307 and 401-404 use a unified QKVParallelLinear with K loaded into the V slot. The adapter generated by scratchpad/ft_research/compute/make_dummy_adapter.py passes discover_adapters / infer_adapter_rank (rank 16) and a peer agent's validate_adapter.py (PASS, with k_eq_v warnings).

findings.question: How noisy is dev evaluation, and how many runs does a decision need?
findings.answer: v3b scored 11, 10 and 8 on dev (1.03–1.09 h per run, 112–119 s per task, about 23.6 tool calls per task). The per-task pass rates over 6 post-fix runs predict a run-to-run SD of about 1.14 tasks; observed SDs are about 1.5. With 3 runs per arm, the SE of the difference is about 1.0–1.2 tasks, so a single comparison can only reliably detect gains of 2.5 tasks or more. Core tasks: 6/6 in all 6 runs. Fixable tasks that ever pass: fastapi_14873 (5/6), fastapi_15589 (5/6), requests_7427 (4/6), fastapi_14791 (3/6), and 4 tasks at 1/6. The remaining 4 fixable tasks never pass.

findings.question: How do data, adapters and runs move between Kaggle, Lightning and the eval notebook?
findings.answer: Use Kaggle as the hub. (1) Data generation runs on Kaggle; traces sit in kernel output, from which you download them, convert them to SFT JSONL, and upload as a private dataset. (2) On Lightning: pip install kaggle, provide a token, then kaggle datasets download for the SFT data and the wheelhouse's vllm wheel, and kaggle models instances versions download for google/gemma-4/transformers/gemma-4-31b-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized (62.6 GB; whole version only, the CLI cannot fetch single files). After training, upload adapters/<name>/{adapter_config.json, adapter_model.safetensors} as a private dataset version. (3) The eval notebook attaches that dataset, but agent_eval needs a small change. kaggle_build refuses to embed .safetensors ('adapters need a Kaggle dataset'). The adapter files therefore have to be copied into runs/<variant>/agent/adapters/ before discover_adapters. Every variant in one notebook must carry the same adapter set, because the server is started from the first variant. For a paired run, put the adapter folder in both variants and reference it (adapter: main_lora) in only one.
findings.evidence: scripts/kaggle_build.py:34 (non-text refused), kaggle/agent_eval/agent_eval.py:55-68 (write_agent_configs), 128-137 (single server and identical-adapter check). kagglesdk ApiDownloadModelInstanceVersionRequest has a 'path' field; I used it to fetch config.json and README.md. The kaggle CLI 2.2.4 has no -f option for models.

compute_eval.recommended_settings:
Files for this work are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaggle-finetune-gemma/16026f0c-2bda-5281-bad9-92d73f9dba6b/scratchpad/ft_research/:
- compute/make_dummy_adapter.py — writes a PEFT adapter from config.json dims with numpy+safetensors only. Uses the correct keys, BF16, lora_A [r,in] / lora_B [out,r], and no v_proj on full-attention layers unless --dup-k-as-v. Tested: r16 = 820 tensors / 234 MiB, r64 = 934 MiB.
- compute/ft0_lora_check.py — draft FT-0 Kaggle script, not pushed.
- model_w4a16/config.json — the served model's config, downloaded from Kaggle.
- my/kag and my/pyp — Kaggle-patched and PyPI vLLM sources, for diffing.

1) FT-0 (one 4xL4 notebook, about 45 min; can run in parallel with data generation)
- Start the server exactly as the scorer path does: adapters = discover_adapters(sub_dir, ALLOWED_ADAPTER_EXTENSIONS); VllmServer(VllmConfig(model=MODEL_PATH, tool_call_parser='gemma4', reasoning_parser='gemma4', max_model_len=32768, dtype='bfloat16', gpu_memory_utilization=G, enable_auto_tool_choice=True, enable_lora=True, max_loras=8, max_lora_rank=128, tensor_parallel_size=4, startup_timeout=1200), adapter_manifest=adapters). build_cmd then emits --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 16.
- Scenarios: S0 (no adapter, G=0.90), S1 (r16 random, 0.90), S2 (r16, 0.80, the HARNESS_README value), optional S3 (r64, 0.90).
- Dummy adapter: python make_dummy_adapter.py <sub>/adapters/ft0_r16 --rank 16 --config $MODEL_PATH/config.json (A ~ N(0,1)/sqrt(in), B ~ N(0,0.02), alpha = 2r).
- Logging: save server._read_captured_output() BEFORE stop(), because stop() deletes the temp log. Grep 'Available KV cache memory', 'GPU KV cache size', 'Maximum concurrency for 32,768'; also /metrics vllm:cache_config_info.
- Tests on each server:
  (a) a 28k-token prompt + 256 output tokens must finish within 600 s, both on the base name (= MODEL_PATH) and on the adapter name (= 'ft0_r16');
  (b) streaming /v1/completions on a ~10k-token prompt, max_tokens 512, ignore_eos, temperature 0, with a fresh nonce prefix each time; 3 reps alternating base and adapter; record TTFT and decode tok/s;
  (c) temperature-0 top-5 logprobs on a fixed prompt, sent as base twice and adapter twice.
- FT-0 PASS needs all of:
  - KV ≥ 32,768 tokens with one r16 adapter at 0.90 (and note the 0.80 value);
  - the 28k prompt completes on both model names;
  - base vs base and adapter vs adapter are deterministic (first-token logprob diff below 1e-3), and base vs adapter differs (text differs or diff > 0.05);
  - adapter decode speed ≥ 85% of S0 base (~36 tok/s reference).
  If S2 (0.80) is below 32,768 but S1 passes, note it as scorer risk and run the adapter eval at 0.80.
- FAIL on any of: adapter not applied, a hang, or KV < 20k at 0.90 → stop the fine-tuning track.

2) GPU budget (4xL4 notebook-hours; the API shows 6 quota-h, next reset Sat 2026-10-10 00:00 UTC; confirm in the UI). If the full 12 h really is available:
- Day 1: FT-0 (0.75 h) in parallel with Gen-A.
- Gen: v3b_noedit prompt on the 72 train tasks, in 2 notebooks in parallel (36 tasks each, K=3–4 samples per task). Use EvalConfig concurrency=2–3 instead of 1, and raise max_time_minutes to ~9 to offset the concurrency slowdown; keep max_tool_calls 40 and max_turns unchanged. Estimate ~2.5 h per notebook, ~5 h total. Sequential would take ~2.4 h per K pass; the concurrency speedup is unmeasured, so log it in the first hour.
- Data gate: at least 60 passing trajectories across at least 15 distinct tasks; otherwise add samples only on tasks that passed at least once.
- Train on Lightning (no Kaggle hours): QLoRA r16, all linear layers, only on language_model.* (exclude the vision tower). Handle k_eq_v as described above. About 1.5–2 h on an A100-80GB or H100, roughly 5 credits (estimate).
- Before spending Kaggle hours, run a parity check on Lightning with the Kaggle vllm wheel (torch 2.10.0). On 3 held-out trajectories, the NLL drop vLLM(W4A16 + adapter) minus base should be at least 50% of the HF/PEFT drop.
- Eval E1: 1 notebook, paired: variant lora then variant base, on the same LoRA-enabled server, dev 33 each, ~2.3 h.
- Eval E2: only if E1 passes. 2 more adapter runs in 2 parallel notebooks, ~2.3 h.
- Total ≈ 0.75 + 5 + 4.6 = 10.4 h, leaving 1.6 h reserve.
- If only about 3 h of 4xL4 wall time are really available: FT-0 plus one Gen notebook (K=2) this week, and eval after the 10-10 reset.
- Plan around 4xL4 queue delays of up to several hours.

3) Decision rules (python scripts/compare_runs.py base=... lora=...)
- Control pool: the 3 existing v3b runs (mean 9.7) plus the paired base run on the LoRA server.
- Early stop after E1: adapter ≤ 7/33, core < 5/6, any overflow or undeclared-tool error, or mean s/task > 140 → no-go.
- GO after 3 adapter runs, all of:
  - adapter mean ≥ control mean + 1.0 (+2 counts as a clear win, ~2 SE);
  - core kept ≥ 17/18;
  - fixable solved mean ≥ control (3.7);
  - malformed ≤ 2 per run, repeat_pct ≤ 6%, overflow = 0, timeouts no worse than control;
  - proj_120_worst_h < 11.
  If adapter is within ±1 of control: no-go. The adapter adds risk (scorer flags, 0.80 gmu, k_eq_v), and the leaderboard cannot resolve ±1.

4) Submission
- Contents: experiments/v3b_noedit plus adapters/main_lora/{adapter_config.json, adapter_model.safetensors} (r16 ≈ 234 MiB, well under 3 GiB), and `adapter: main_lora` on the root agent only.
- Checks: scripts/build_submission.py (official compile) and validate_adapter.py.
- One submission per day. Treat the leaderboard result as weak evidence (±2.5 tasks); v3b's reference is 0.12 = 7/58.
- For the 2 final selections, keep one adapter-free config (v3b) as a hedge.
risks: Quota mismatch: the API says 6 GPU-hours this week (reset Saturday 00:00 UTC); the brief says ~12 h. If 4xL4 costs double, only ~3 h of 4xL4 wall time are available, which is not enough for data generation plus 3 eval runs this week.

The scorer's gpu_memory_utilization is unknown: HARNESS_README says 0.80, the official notebook says 0.90. At 0.80, KV with one adapter is estimated at 28k–36k tokens and could fall below 32,768. FT-0 must measure it.

k_eq_v train/serve mismatch: on the 10 full-attention layers, a k_proj LoRA trained in HF also changes V, but in vLLM it only reaches K. Fix by duplicating it as v_proj or by not targeting k_proj on those layers.

Plain PyPI vLLM 0.19.1 cannot serve LoRA on Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration. Any vLLM use off Kaggle (parity checks, data generation on Lightning) must install the patched wheel from the Kaggle wheelhouse, with torch==2.10.0.

Training base differs from the served base: the bf16 QAT-unquantized or bitsandbytes-4bit training model is not the W4A16 compressed-tensors served model. Effects may shrink; check with the parity test.

Concurrency >1 during data generation slows each LLM call, which may shift the trajectory distribution (more time-outs). Raise max_time_minutes for generation only, and keep tool and turn budgets identical.
Dev noise (SE ~1 task with 3 runs per arm) cannot detect gains under ~2.5 tasks. The expected FT gain (+0 to +2) is at or below what we can resolve.

findings.question: What changed in the vLLM wheel between the 10-03 copy and the 10-12 wheelhouse?
findings.answer: Only one source file changed: vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py. The patch adds "vision_embedder." to the skip list in Gemma4ForCausalLM.load_weights, which lets the 12B checkpoint load. Nothing under vllm/lora/*, gemma4_mm.py, the registry, the reasoning parsers or the tool parsers changed. For reference, the full set of organizer patches compared with PyPI vllm 0.19.1 is lora/model_manager.py, gemma4.py and gemma4_mm.py. These were already in the 09-30/10-03 copy (except the vision_embedder line): the SupportsLoRA mixin on Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration, the MoE LoRA mapping, de-duplicated module registration (so LoRA layers are not wrapped twice), and a fix so that activating an adapter does not reset a shared module.

findings.question: Does the patched vLLM Gemma4ForCausalLM (the class the 12B is served with via hf-overrides) support LoRA, and what key naming does it expect?
findings.answer: Yes. The class is declared as Gemma4ForCausalLM(nn.Module, SupportsLoRA, SupportsPP, MixtureOfExperts, SupportsEagle3) and packs q/k/v into qkv_proj and gate/up into gate_up_proj. Its hf_to_vllm_mapper rewrites 'model.language_model.' to 'model.', and WorkerLoRAManager passes that mapper to LoRAModel.from_local_checkpoint. PEFT keys produced by the HF multimodal wrapper therefore work: base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.{self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj, mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj}.lora_{A,B}.weight. Keys from the text-only HF class (base_model.model.model.layers.N...) also map. The adapter must contain only language-model linears. vLLM raises ValueError for any module whose last name component is not an expected LoRA module, so PEFT 'all-linear' would break loading by also catching vision_embedder.patch_dense or embed_vision/embed_audio.embedding_projection. The k_eq_v caveat is the same as on 31B. vLLM copies K weights into the V slot of qkv_proj, but a PEFT adapter has no v_proj on full-attention layers, so the V slot gets no LoRA delta, while HF computes V = k_proj(x) including the delta. The k_proj LoRA must be duplicated as v_proj on the full layers. The existing ft_research/fix_k_eq_v.py hardcodes glob=range(5,60,6) for 31B; 12B needs range(5,48,6), which is 8 layers.
findings.evidence: new gemma4.py:1439-1474 (class, mapper, packed_modules_mapping) and 1572-1590, 1649-1660 (K duplicated into V for k_eq_v layers). lora/worker_manager.py:128-145 (weights_mapper=hf_to_vllm_mapper). lora/lora_model.py:161-191 (unexpected-module ValueError). LoRA QKV slicing with KV-head replication: lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py:312-338 (kv_shard_id = tp_rank // num_kv_head_replicas), which covers the 12B's 1 global KV head under TP4. Not run on GPU.

findings.question: CRITICAL: did the thinking semantics change for configs with include_thoughts: false (all our configs, including v3b_noedit)?
findings.answer: Yes. Our 'thinking off' config now runs with thinking ON. build_submission_limits sets the generation default thinking_config {thinking_budget: 4096}, and GenerationConstraints.validate_config deep-merges it into the user's thinking_config. v3b_noedit therefore resolves to {thinking_budget: 4096, include_thoughts: false}. In 0.2.12, include_thoughts False was checked first, so this meant enable_thinking=False. In 0.2.13 the budget/level is checked first, so it means enable_thinking=True with thinking_token_budget=4096, and include_thoughts:false now only strips thought parts from ADK history and drops reasoning/reasoning_content from outgoing messages. To really disable thinking you must now set thinking_budget: 0 (or thinking_level: none). Any dev run or submission made on the 10-12 wheelhouse with our current configs thinks for up to 4096 tokens per call. That changes timing (about 8.7 s per call per forum 746250) and is the behaviour the training data has to match.
findings.evidence: Simulated with the real code (kwh_1012/scripts/think_check.py, venv312 python). Old: 0.2.12 {'include_thoughts': False} -> merged {'thinking_budget': 4096, 'include_thoughts': False} -> extra_body {'chat_template_kwargs': {'enable_thinking': False}}. New: 0.2.13, same input -> {'chat_template_kwargs': {'enable_thinking': True}, 'thinking_token_budget': 4096}, with _adk_include_thoughts=False. With thinking_budget 0, both versions give enable_thinking False. Code: adk_submission/resolvers/generation.py (new) 400-419 (order of checks), 426-429, 433-447. limits.py:400-445 (default merge plus budget auto-fill). swegemma/config.py:59-67 (defaults {'max_output_tokens': 16384, 'thinking_config': {'thinking_budget': 4096}}). experiments/v3b_noedit/configs/sampling.yaml:9-12 (only include_thoughts: false). Whether the scorer uses the same build_submission_limits defaults is likely but not confirmed; our dev kernel imports it at kaggle/agent_eval/agent_eval.py:166.

findings.question: What else changed in adk_submission's thinking handling (history stripping)?
findings.answer: New in 0.2.13, when include_thoughts is False: (1) LiteLlm.generate_content_async is wrapped to remove Part(thought=True) from responses before they enter session history, and partial streaming chunks that contain only thoughts are skipped. (2) _get_completion_inputs strips 'reasoning' and 'reasoning_content' from outgoing assistant messages, where earlier versions mirrored reasoning_content into reasoning. When include_thoughts is True or unset, the old mirroring still runs, so earlier thoughts are re-sent to vLLM on later steps.
findings.evidence: generation.py (new) 80-90 _strip_reasoning_from_messages, 93-117 _extract_include_thoughts, 120-143 _strip_thought_parts_from_response, 270-280 (strip vs normalize), 305-335 (patched generate_content_async).

findings.question: What changed in swegemma 0.2.7 -> 0.2.11 (agent_runner, evaluate, config, verification, timing)?
findings.answer:
evaluate.py is unchanged. Compaction is not configured anywhere in swegemma: events_compaction_config is still passed through from the scorer (agent_runner.py:694-695), so the threshold question (32768 vs 14336, forum 748584) is unresolved. Changes:
(a) A new ToolErrorPlugin is installed on every run. Undeclared-tool calls and tool exceptions now come back to the model as {'status':'error',...} instead of ending the task. ADK 1.36.1 routes a 'Tool not found' ValueError through on_tool_error_callback. The repo comment in agent.yaml that an undeclared tool call scores 0 is now stale.
(b) The task prompt changed. The workspace tree is now breadth-first, maxdepth 3, prunes docs/tests/examples/benchmarks/etc., and holds 200 lines (previously 150 lines unpruned). The read_file limit lines and the graph tools section only list tools the agent actually declares, and the graph tool wording now says to query by dotted symbol path. Docstrings in tools/graph.py changed to match.
(c) Patches are filtered. submit_patch, the unsubmitted-diff fallback and Phase-2 verification all drop diff sections that touch conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, *.pth, test_*.py, *_test.py, any .py under a tests/test/testing dir, or the task's test_files.
(d) Phase-2 verification has its own timeout, verification_timeout_seconds (default 300 s). Previously it used command_timeout_seconds (our timeout_seconds 180). So eval_config timeout_seconds no longer bounds the hidden-test run, and the comment in v3b_noedit/eval_config.yaml is stale. Whether the scorer overrides 300 is unknown.
(e) Unexpected exceptions inside the sandbox run are caught and reported as 'Sandbox execution error' instead of propagating.
(f) Skill-tool list arguments are coerced.
(g) BREAKING for our dev kernel: swegemma/models/discovery.py and registry.py were removed (validate_single_declared_model, setup_gemma_model_registry, resolve_swegemma_adapter moved into agent_runner). kaggle/agent_eval/agent_eval.py:87 does 'from swegemma.models.discovery import validate_single_declared_model' and will raise ModuleNotFoundError on the current wheelhouse. findings.question: 12B architecture: what is it, and does it have k_eq_v layers?
findings.answer: gemma-4-12b-it ('12B Unified', 11.95B params) uses architectures Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration and model_type gemma4_unified. It is a dense text decoder with no vision or audio towers, only small vision_embedder/embed_vision/embed_audio linears. Text config: 48 layers, hidden 3840, intermediate 15360, 16 query heads, sliding layers with 8 KV heads × head_dim 256 and window 1024, full-attention layers every 6th (idx 5,11,...,47; 8 layers) with global_head_dim 512 and num_global_key_value_heads 1. attention_k_eq_v is true: the full layers have no v_proj in any checkpoint. Also: vocab 262144 with tied embeddings, a per-layer layer_scalar, no PLE, no MoE, partial_rotary 0.25 proportional RoPE on full layers. For comparison, 31B is 60 layers, hidden 5376, 32 heads, 16 KV / 4 global KV, intermediate 21504, 10 full layers, also k_eq_v. Checkpoint tensor names are model.language_model.layers.N.* in all three 12B variants. The W4A16 CT file (10.26 GB) has int4 group-32 symmetric linears (6.13 GB) plus bf16 embed_tokens (2.01 GB) and a separate bf16 lm_head (2.01 GB), which vLLM skips because the embeddings are tied. The chat template is the same as 31B apart from an image/audio/video placeholder loop in tool bodies. transformers 5.13.1 (wheelhouse) includes models/gemma4_unified. Its text attention is the gemma4 one: v_proj=None on k_eq_v layers and value=key, plus v_norm.

findings.question: How much faster or cheaper would 12B training and serving be than 31B?
findings.answer: These are estimates, not measured. Params are 11.95B vs 30.7B, so training FLOPs per token are about 2.6x lower (roughly 7.2e10 vs 1.8e11). Memory is the bigger win. A 12B QLoRA (nf4 linears ~5.8 GB + bf16 embeddings 2 GB, about 8 GB) fits on a single 24 GB L4 with LoRA and Adam states plus gradient-checkpointed activations at ~8-16k tokens, so 4xL4 can run 4-way data parallel. 31B nf4 is about 20 GB and needs pipeline/device_map sharding with one GPU active at a time. Expected training throughput on 4xL4 is therefore about 5-10x higher for 12B. Bf16 LoRA of 12B (24 GB) fits sharded across 2-4 L4s. Long sequences still need chunked or fused cross-entropy, because 262k-vocab logits at 16k tokens are 8.6 GB in bf16. Whether head_dim-512 attention gets an efficient SDPA kernel is unknown (earlier sdp_utils investigation). Adapter size (all 7 linears, language model only): 12B is about 4.10M params per rank unit, so r=64 is ~0.52 GB and r=128 ~1.05 GB in bf16; 31B is about 7.65M per rank unit, ~0.98 GB at r=64. Serving: per-decode-token weight reads are about 8 GB vs about 21 GB (both include a 2-2.8 GB bf16 lm_head), so roughly 2-2.6x faster decode and prefill. Per GPU under TP4, weights are about 2.6 GB vs about 5.8 GB. Full-attention KV is about 16 KB/token vs about 82 KB/token, and sliding KV is bounded at 1024 tokens in both. Quality: model-card coding scores are lower (LiveCodeBench v6 72.0 vs 80.0, Codeforces 1659 vs 2150, Tau2 69.0 vs 76.9). SWE-style resolve rate for 12B, with or without LoRA, is unknown.
